ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r3.claim: Money given as usury to increase wealth does not grow with God or receive blessing; the author links this to the statement that God erases usury and nurtures charity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r3.anchor: فلا يزكو عند الله، ولا يبارك فيه لقوله: يمحق الله الربا ويربي الصدقات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r4.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says the verse was revealed about Thaqīf's usurious dealings with Quraysh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r4.anchor: قال السدي: نزلت في ربا ثقيف، كانوا يعملون بالربا، ويعمله فيهم قريش.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Ibn Jubayr, and Ṭāwūs say the verse concerns gifts given in expectation of a return.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وابن جبير، وطاوس: هذه الآية نزلت في هبات، للثواب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya extends the gift interpretation to similar reciprocal arrangements: they are not sinful but bring no divine reward or increase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وما جرى مجراهما مما يصنع للمجازاة، كالسلم وغيره، فهو وإن كان لا إثم فيه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والنخعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Nakhaʿī interpret the verse as gifts to relatives or brothers intended to benefit and finance them; any increase accrues to the recipients.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا، والنخعي: نزلت في قوم يعطون قراباتهم وإخوانهم على معنى نفعهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r8.speaker: الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r8.claim: Al-Shaʿbī gives a similar interpretation: when someone serves another and the other benefits, that benefit belongs to the recipient.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r8.anchor: وقال الشعبي قريبا من هذا وهو: أن ما خدم به الإنسان غيره انتفع به، فذلك النفع لهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r9.claim: The author prefers the first interpretation: the passage prohibits usury.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r9.anchor: والظاهر القول الأول، وهو النهي عن الربا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r10.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r10.claim: Most readers lengthen the initial hamza in “what you give,” meaning what you grant; Ibn Kathīr shortens it, meaning what you bring.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وما آتيتم، الأول بمد الهمزة، أي وما أعطيتم وابن كثير: بقصرها، أي وما جئتم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r11.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r11.claim: Most read “to increase” with yāʾ, attributing the increase to usury; several authorities read it with feminine tāʾ, attributing it to the gifts, while Abū Mālik adds a feminine object suffix.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r11.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ليربو، بالياء وإسناد الفعل إلى الربا وابن عباس، والحسن، وقتادة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r12.claim: “Those who multiply” means people whose reward is multiplied; al-Farrāʾ compares the form to words meaning owners of fat or thirsty camels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r12.anchor: والمضعف: ذو أضعاف في الأجر. قال الفراء: هم أصحاب المضاعفة، كما تقول:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r13.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r13.claim: Ubayy reads “the multiplied” with fatḥa on the ʿayn, as a passive participle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r13.anchor: وقرأ أبي: المضعفون، بفتح العين، اسم مفعول.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī hears a rhetorical shift to God's angels and chosen creatures, and supplies an omitted complement: the donors are multiplied in reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r14.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فأولئك هم المضعفون، التفات حسن، كأنه قال لملائكته وخواص خلقه:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r15.claim: The author says al-Zamakhsharī's reading is easier to construe, but the first interpretation carries more benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p393/r15.anchor: وهذا أسهل مأخذا، والأول أملأ بالفائدة

DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r3.claim: The worldly seeker receives the reward of his deed here but nothing in the Hereafter; Sa'id compares this to the verse about usury not growing with God.
DURR-FULL:v4p407#2/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه {من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها نوف إليهم أعمالهم فيها وهم فيها لا يبخسون} قال: يؤتون ثواب ما عملوا

STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r11.claim: After challenging disbelievers to substantiate their claims, the sūrah treats kinship rights, just use of wealth, human life phases, and corruption.
STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r11.anchor: Challenging the disbelievers to bring something to substantiate their claims (v. 35), the sūrah then touches upon several broader Quranic themes

QURTUBI-FULL:19:54-55#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:54-55#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:54-55#3/r1.claim: The verse's spelling of ribā with wāw supports al-Zajjaj's correction that it should not be written with yāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:54-55#3/r1.anchor: ومآ آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس

SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r1.claim: The common reading has open ياء and makes الربا the subject, meaning it increases; here واو is part of the word.
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r1.anchor: العامة على الياء من تحت مفتوحة، أسند الفعل لضمير الربا أي: ليزداد.

SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r2.speaker: نافع
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r2.claim: Nafi reads with addressed plural تاء; واو is then the pronoun suffix for an absent plural subject.
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r2.anchor: ونافع بتاء من فوق مضمومة خطابا للجماعة. فالواو على الأول لام كلمة، وعلى الثاني كلمة ضمير لغائبين.

SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r3.claim: The author notes that long and short readings of آتيتم were discussed earlier in al-Baqara.
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r3.anchor: وقد تقدمت قراءتا " آتيتم " بالمد والقصر في البقرة.

SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r4.claim: المضعفون means people possessing multiples; al-Farra' compares the pattern to owners of fat or thirsty camels. Ubayy reads it with open عين as a passive participle.
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r4.anchor: قوله: " المضعفون " أي: أصحاب الأضعاف. قال الفراء: " نحو مسمن، ومعطش أي: ذي إبل سمان وإبل عطاش "

SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies a resumptive pronoun for the non-adverbial conditional; alternatively, the author says the omitted phrase فمؤتوه is easier, while the first reading offers more benefit.
SAMIN-DURR:30:39/r5.anchor: يعني أن اسم الشرط متى كان غير ظرف وجب عود ضمير من الجواب عليه. وتقدم ذلك في البقرة عند قوله: قل من كان عدوا لجبريل

ZAJJAJ:v4p187/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p187/r3.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p187/r3.claim: Most exegesis treats a gift made to receive a larger return as not forbidden, though it earns no reward for the excess received.
ZAJJAJ:v4p187/r3.anchor: فذلك في أكثر التفسير ليس بحرام، ولكنه لا ثواب لمن زاد على ما أخذ.

ZAJJAJ:v4p187/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p187/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p187/r4.claim: There are two kinds of increase: a forbidden loan requiring a larger repayment or benefit, and a permissible gift or present offered in hope of receiving more.
ZAJJAJ:v4p187/r4.anchor: والربا ربوان، والحرام كل قرض يؤخذ به أكثر منه أو يجر منفعة، فهذا حرام، والذي ليس بحرام هو الذي يهبه الإنسان

ZAJJAJ:v4p187#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p187#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p187#2/r1.claim: This is charity given without seeking repayment, directed instead toward God's reward.
ZAJJAJ:v4p187#2/r1.anchor: أي وما أعطيتم من صدقة لا تطلبون بها المكافأة وإنما يقصدون بها ما عند الله.

ZAJJAJ:v4p187#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p187#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p187#2/r2.claim: Those who give such charity receive multiplied reward: tenfold for a good deed, with further increase as God wills.
ZAJJAJ:v4p187#2/r2.anchor: أي فأهلها هم المضعفون، أي هم الذي يضاعف لهم الثواب. يعطون بالحسنة عشرة أمثالها ويضاعف الله لمن يشاء،

ZAJJAJ:v4p187#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p187#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p187#2/r3.claim: Morphologically, مُضعِف means a possessor of multiple rewards, like مُقوٍ meaning strong and مُوسر meaning wealthy.
ZAJJAJ:v4p187#2/r3.anchor: وقيل (المضعفون) كما يقال رجل مقو، أي صاحب قوة، وموسر أي صاحب يسار، وكذلك مضعف، أي ذو أضعاف من الحسنات

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r1.claim: This is the earliest Qur'anic revelation to mention the term and concept of riba.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r1.anchor: This is the earliest mention of the term and concept of riba in the chronology of Qur'anic revelation.

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r2.claim: In ordinary linguistic usage, riba means an addition or increase beyond a thing's original amount.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r2.anchor: In its general, linguistic sense, this term denotes an "addition" to or an "increase" of a thing

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r3.claim: In Qur'anic terminology, riba is an unlawful interest addition to money or goods lent by one person or group to another.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r3.anchor: in the terminology of the Qur'an, it signifies any unlawful addition, by way of interest, to a sum of money or goods lent

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r4.speaker: most of the early Muslim jurists
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r4.claim: Early jurists generally treated unlawful riba as profits from any interest-bearing loan, whatever the rate or economic motive.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r4.anchor: most of the early Muslim jurists identified this "unlawful addition" with profits obtained through any kind of interest-bearing loans

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r5.speaker: Islamic scholars
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r5.claim: Islamic scholars have not reached a comprehensive definition of riba that covers every legal case and changing economic need.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r5.anchor: Islamic scholars have not yet been able to reach an absolute agreement on the definition of riba

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r6.speaker: Ibn Kathir
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir calls riba one of the most difficult topics for scholars.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r6.anchor: In the words of Ibn Kathir (in his commentary on 2:275), "the subject of riba is one

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r7.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r7.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r7.claim: The legal condemnation and prohibition in 2:275–281 was the Prophet's final revelation, received only days before his death.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r7.anchor: the passage condemning and prohibiting riba in legal terms (2:275-281) was the last revelation received by the Prophet, who died a few days later

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r8.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r8.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r8.claim: Because this legal passage came at the end of the Prophet's life, the Companions had no chance to ask him about its legal implications.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r8.anchor: the Companions had no opportunity to ask him about the shar'i implications of the relevant injunction

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r9.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r9.speaker: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r9.claim: Umar said the final revelation on riba was left unexplained by the Prophet; Asad cites Ibn Hanbal through Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r9.anchor: even 'Umar ibn al-Khattab is reliably reported to have said: "The last [of the Qur'an) that was revealed

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r10.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r10.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r10.claim: The Quran's severe condemnation, viewed alongside later economic experience, sufficiently shows riba's nature and social and moral effects.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r10.anchor: the severity with which the Qur'an condemns riba and those who practice it furnishes - especially when viewed against the background of mankind's economic experiences

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r11.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r11.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r11.claim: Riba's blame attaches to interest loans exploiting weaker borrowers: lenders retain ownership and guaranteed gain regardless of how funds are used or whether borrowers lose.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r11.anchor: the opprobrium of riba (in the sense in which this term is used in the Qur'an and in many sayings of the Prophet) attaches to profits

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r12.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r12.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r12.claim: Classifying transactions as riba is ultimately a moral question tied to the socioeconomic motives shaping the lender-borrower relationship.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r12.anchor: the question as to what kinds of financial transactions fall within the category of riba is, in the last resort, a moral one

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r13.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r13.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r13.claim: Economically, the issue is how borrowers and lenders can share profits and risks equitably.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r13.anchor: it is a question as to how profits and risks may be equitably shared by both partners to a loan transaction

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r14.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r14.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r14.claim: No fixed answer can cover all eras; successive generations must reinterpret riba as social, technological, and economic conditions change.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r14.anchor: our answers must necessarily vary in accordance with the changes to which man's social and technological development - and, thus, his economic environment - is subject

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r15.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r15.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r15.claim: Although riba's condemnation is final and unequivocal, this early mention stops short of a clear legal prohibition and foreshadows the later ban through its condemnation of exploiting others' possessions.
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n35/r15.anchor: the Qur'anic condemnation of the concept and practice of riba is unequivocal and final, every successive Muslim generation

ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n36/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n36/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:38#n36/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to 2:276 for a related statement about riba.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r1.claim: All readers lengthen ātiytum in the first clause except Ibn Kathir, who shortens it; all agree on the long form in the zakāt clause.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r1.anchor: كلهم قرأ: وما آتيتم من ربا [الروم/ 39] ممدودا غير ابن كثير فإنه قرأ: (أتيتم) قصرا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r2.claim: The phrase refers to a gift made in expectation of a larger return; it does not grow with God because the donor seeks compensation rather than God's favor, as in the warning not to give expecting more.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r2.anchor: معنى وما آتيتم من ربا: ما آتيتم من هدية أهديتموها لتعوضوا ما هو أكثر منها

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r3.claim: The long form ātiytum means gave, as in آتاهم الله; the short form means came or did, but yields the same sense because coming to it is giving it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r3.anchor: فمن مد آتيتم، فلأن المعنى: أعطيتم من قوله: فآتاهم الله ثواب الدنيا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r4.speaker: الشاعر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r4.claim: The cited poem أتيت الذي يأتي السفيه uses ataytu for doing what a fool does, supporting the short form's sense of acting or coming to something.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r4.anchor: أتيت الذي يأتي السفيه لغرتي ... إلى أن علا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r5.claim: There is no disagreement over lengthening ātiytum in the clause about zakāt.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p446/r5.anchor: ولم يختلفوا في مد وما آتيتم من زكاة

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r1.speaker: كلهم غير نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r1.claim: All readers except Nāfiʿ read ليربو with yāʾ; the source gives no separate semantic explanation for this form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r1.anchor: وكلهم قرأ: ليربوا في أموال الناس

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r2.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ reads لتربو with tāʾ, with the wāw quiescent.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r2.anchor: غير نافع، فإنه قرأ (لتربو) بالتاء، ساكنة الواو

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r3.claim: Al-Fārisī says the gift is called riba figuratively because it seeks an increase; strictly, riba is the forbidden excess taken above what was given.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r3.anchor: والمدفوع ليس في الحقيقة ربا، إنما المحرم الزيادة التي يأخذها زائدا على ما أعطى

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r4.claim: Gifts intended to attract reciprocation increase among people but bring no increase with God; a gift given for God's sake instead resembles zakat and earns multiplied reward.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p447#2/r4.anchor: فلا يربو عند الله، لأنه لم يقصد به وجه البر والقربة، إنما قصد به اجتلاب الزيادة

NASHR:v2p74/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p74/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p74/r1.claim: A reported pause on وما آتيتم من ربا uses yāʾ.
NASHR:v2p74/r1.anchor: والوقف على وما آتيتم من ربا بالياء

NASHR:v2p74/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p74/r3.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v2p74/r3.claim: Al-Dānī says this is the only explicit transmission he found from Warsh; several authorities report consensus on the practice.
NASHR:v2p74/r3.anchor: قال الداني: ولم يأت به عن ورش نصا غيره. انتهى. وممن حكى الإجماع على هذا

NASHR:v2p74/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p74/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p74/r4.claim: The author says this is the performance he learned from most teachers and the only one known to him, and judges it the sound analogy.
NASHR:v2p74/r4.anchor: وأما الأداء فهو الذي قرأنا به على عامة شيوخنا، ولم نعلم أحدا أخذ علي سواه، وهو القياس الصحيح

NASHR:v2p74/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p74/r5.speaker: الشاطبي والسخاوي
NASHR:v2p74/r5.claim: Some performance authorities report unrestricted fatḥ on tanwīn at pause for readers who use imāla, or a between-vowels form; the author knows no qirāʾāt authority who adopted it.
NASHR:v2p74/r5.anchor: وقد ذهب بعض أهل الأداء إلى حكاية الفتح في المنون مطلقا من ذلك في الوقف عمن أمال

NASHR:v2p74/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p74/r6.speaker: المازني
NASHR:v2p74/r6.claim: Al-Māzinī holds that the pause alif replaces tanwīn in all case endings, since tanwīn after fatḥa becomes alif at pause regardless of grammatical case.
NASHR:v2p74/r6.anchor: فحكي عن المازني أنها بدل من التنوين سواء كان الاسم مرفوعا، أو منصوبا، أو مجرورا

NASHR:v2p74/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p74/r7.speaker: الكسائي والكوفيون وبعض البصريين
NASHR:v2p74/r7.claim: They hold that pause alif restores the word’s original final letter, dropped in connection because it meets tanwīn; al-Dānī attributes this view to Kufans and some Basrans.
NASHR:v2p74/r7.anchor: وحكي عن الكسائي، وغيره أن هذه الألف ليست بدلا من التنوين، وإنما هي بدل من لام الكلمة

NASHR:v2p74/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p74/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p74/r8.claim: The author rejects the unrestricted tanwīn-opening position as a grammatical analogy rather than a transmitted recitation and says it appears in no qirāʾāt manual.
NASHR:v2p74/r8.anchor: وإنما هو مذهب نحوي لا أدائي دعا إليه القياس لا الرواية، وذلك أن النحاة اختلفوا

NASHR:v2p344#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p344#2/r4.speaker: المدنيان ويعقوب
NASHR:v2p344#2/r4.claim: The two Medinans and Yaʿqūb address the audience, with tāʾ carrying damma and wāw quiescent; the others use third person with fatḥa on yāʾ and wāw.
NASHR:v2p344#2/r4.anchor: قرأ المدنيان ويعقوب بالخطاب وضم التاء، وإسكان الواو، وقرأ الباقون بالغيب وفتح الياء والواو

NASHR:v2p344#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p344#2/r5.speaker: القراء
NASHR:v2p344#2/r5.claim: All readers agree on madd in وما آتيتم من زكاة, supported by the Qurʾanic expression إيتاء الزكاة.
NASHR:v2p344#2/r5.anchor: مد: وما آتيتم من زكاة من أجل قوله تعالى: وإيتاء الزكاة

QIRAAT-ER:30:39:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:30:39:3#1/r1.speaker: Vr
QIRAAT-ER:30:39:3#1/r1.claim: Form I ataytum means “you brought,” unlike Form IV ātaytum, “you gave”; the variant shifts agency from granting to carrying.
QIRAAT-ER:30:39:3#1/r1.anchor: Vr, mutawatir: "Form I reading (ataytum, ""you came with/brought"") instead of Form IV (ātaytum, ""you gave

QIRAAT-ER:30:39:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:30:39:7#1/r1.speaker: Imp
QIRAAT-ER:30:39:7#1/r1.claim: The second-person plural reading makes the givers the active subject increasing the sum, rather than ribā growing by itself.
QIRAAT-ER:30:39:7#1/r1.anchor: Imp, mutawatir: 2nd person plural (you [all] increase it) — shifts subject from ribā growing on its own

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies this non-rewarded riba as a gift given in expectation of a greater return; its giver earns neither reward nor sin.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى ﴿ وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس ﴾ قال هي هدية الرجل يهدي الشيء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses zakah as charity; those who give it seeking God’s face are the ones whose reward is multiplied.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r2.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى ﴿ وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس ﴾ قال هي هدية الرجل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r3.claim: Mujahid gives the same explanation: the gift is made in expectation of a better return, but brings neither reward nor sin.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r4.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak calls this permissible riba: a gift intended to bring a better return, for which the giver earns neither reward nor sin.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p103#3/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم في قوله تعالى ﴿ وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس ﴾ قال هو الربا الحلال

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r1.speaker: الجبائي والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r1.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī, and a report from al-Ḥasan, take riba in its familiar sense of the prohibited transactional increase.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r1.anchor: الظاهر أنه أريد به الزيادة المعروفة في المعاملة التي حرمها الشارع وإليه ذهب الجبائي وروى ذلك عن الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r2.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says the verse was revealed about the usury practiced by Thaqīf; Quraysh practiced it as well, supporting the conventional-usury interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r2.anchor: ويشهد له ما روى عن السدي من أن الآية نزلت في ربا ثقيف كانوا يربون وكذا كانت قريش

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك ومحمد بن كعب القرظي وطاوس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, Ṭāwūs, and others interpret it as a gift given in expectation of a greater return; riba is figurative because it causes increase or is an unowed excess.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r3.anchor: وعن إبن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك ومحمد بن كعب القرظي وطاوس وغيرهم أنه أريد به العطية التي يتوقع بها مزيد مكافأة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r4.speaker: النخعي وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r4.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī, also in a report from Ibn ʿAbbās, says the verse concerns gifts to relatives and brothers meant to help them and increase their wealth, with the gift itself called riba by the same figurative reasoning.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r4.anchor: وعن النخعي أن الآية نزلت في قوم يعطون قراباتهم وإخوانهم على معنى نفعهم وتمويلهم والتفضيل عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r5.claim: Whichever interpretation of riba is adopted, min is explanatory rather than causal.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#2/r5.anchor: وجه تسميتها بما ذكر معلوم مما ذكرنا وأياما كانفمن بيانلما لا للتعليل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the verb without the long vowel, meaning what you bring; in the majority reading it means what you give.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r1.anchor: قرأ إبن كثير ( أتيتم ) بالقصر ومعناه على قراءة الجمهور أعطيتم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r2.claim: On the usual reading, the gift or riba increases and grows within the recipients' wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r2.anchor: أي ليزيد ذلك الربا ويزكو في أموال الناس الذين آتيتموهم إياه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r3.speaker: ابن الشيخ
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r3.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says that when riba means a gift, it grows by attracting people's money and drawing some of it to the giver through the gift.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r3.anchor: وقال إبن الشيخ : المعنى عل ى تفسير الربا بالعطية ليزيد ذلك الربا في جذب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة وأبي رجاء والشعبي ونافع ويعقوب وأبي حيوة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r4.claim: These authorities read liturbū with second-person tāʾ and ḍamma: the understood object may be the gift, people's wealth, or the phrase may express becoming possessed of riba in their wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r4.anchor: وعن إبن عباس والحسن وقتادة وأبي رجاء والشعبي ونافع ويعقوب وأبي حيوة ( لتربوا )

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r5.claim: On the tāʾ reading, the verb can be causative with an omitted object, transitive to people's wealth, or resultative: that the givers become people of riba in others' wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r5.anchor: وإسناد الفعل إليهم وهو باب الأفعال المتعدية لواحد بهمزة التعدية والمفعول محذوف أي لتربوه وتزيدوه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r6.speaker: أبو مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r6.claim: Abū Mālik reads liturbūhā with a feminine pronoun referring to riba understood as a gift or similar thing.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو مالك ( لتربوها ) بضمير المؤنث وكان الضمير للربا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r7.claim: It does not increase with God means that God does not bless it in His reckoning and judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r7.anchor: أي فلا يبارك فيه في تقديره تعالى وحكمه عزوجل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r8.claim: Zakat here means charity, given with the sincere aim of seeking God's countenance.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r9.claim: Al-muḍʿifūn can mean people who become possessors of multiplied return, since their gift's reward is doubled, like someone who becomes strong or wealthy.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r9.anchor: أي ذوو الإضعاف على أن مضعفا أسم فاعل من أضعف أي صار ذا ضعف بكسر فسكون بأن يضاعف له ثواب ما أعطاه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r10.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r10.claim: An alternative derives al-muḍʿifūn causatively, those who multiply their reward and wealth through zakat's blessing; Ubayy's passive reading supports this analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من أضعف والهمزة للتعدية والمفعول محذوف أي الذين ضعفوا ثوابهم وأموالهم ببركة الزكاة ويؤيد هذا الوجه قراءة أبي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r11.claim: The verse replaces the expected it grows with God with a nominal sentence about them; the demonstrative, pronoun of separation, and nominal form intensify and restrict the promised multiplication to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r11.anchor: إذ أثبت غير ما قبله وفي النظم إذ أتى فيما قبل بجملة فعلية وهنا بجملة أسمية مصدرة بأسم الإشارة مع ضمير الفصل لقصد المبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r12.claim: The demonstrative honors the givers and the shift away from direct address exalts their state, as if God were informing the angels and elect about them.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r12.anchor: والإلتفات عن الخطاب حيث قيل : فأولئك دون فأنتم للتعظيم كأنه سبحانه خاطب بذلك الملائكة عليهم السلام وخواص الخلق

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r13.claim: The hidden referent before the predicate may be the givers or those who gave; the wording can be general if those refers to them and others, and the author prefers construing it as the predicate's referent.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r13.anchor: والراجح في الكلام إلى ( ما ) محذوف أن جعلت موصولة وكذلك إن جعلت شرطية

ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r14.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r14.claim: Al-Kashshāf says the shifted construction better serves the praise meant to encourage giving: the demonstrative honors the donors, praises them before angels, makes a graceful shift, and adds the benefit illustrated by a cited line.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p45#3/r14.anchor: وفي الكشاف أن الكلام عليه أملا بالفائدة وبين ذلك بأن الكلام مسوق لمدح المؤتين حثا في الفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r1.claim: Under the conventional-usury interpretation, this verse matches the teaching that God erases usury and nurtures charitable gifts.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r1.anchor: والآية على المعنى الأول للربا في معنى قوله عزوجل : أيمحق الله الربا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r2.claim: The cited poetic line fa-dhālika an yahlika fa-ḥasbī thanāʾuhu illustrates the additional rhetorical value of the demonstrative in the shifted construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r2.anchor: فذلك أن يهلك فحسبي ثناؤه بخلافه إذا جعل وصفا للمؤتين

ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r3.speaker: كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r3.claim: Many scholars say the verse implies a prohibition of transactional riba; Alusi argues that such an implication would also reach the gift-for-recompense interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r3.anchor: والذي يقتضيه كلام كثير أنها تشعر بالنهي عن الربا بذلك المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r4.claim: Scholars explicitly say a gift expecting extra repayment is not unlawful for others, though it is forbidden to the Prophet under the command not to give expecting more.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r4.anchor: مع أنهم صرحوا بعدم حرمة ذلك على غيره صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وحرمتها عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r5.claim: The recipient's added repayment is lawful and its giver is not sinful, but neither that repayment nor the original gift earns reward because the former is compensation and the latter a snare.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r5.anchor: وكذا صرحوا بأن ما يأخذه المعطي لتلك العطية من الزيادة على ما أعطاه ليس بحرام ودافعه ليس بآثم لكنه لا يثاب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r6.speaker: بعض التابعين
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r6.claim: Some Successors say the person who gives generously in expectation of more is rewarded from the gift: when a stranger gives to elicit a greater return, reciprocate and add to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p46/r6.anchor: ومعنى قول بعض التابعين الجانب المستغزر يثاب من هبته أن الرجل الغريب إذا أهدى إليك شيئا لتكافئه وتزيده شيئا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r11.speaker: ابن كثير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir reads ataytum with a short initial vowel, meaning what you brought of usury as a gift.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r12.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r12.claim: Other readers lengthen the form to mean what you gave of usury.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r13.claim: The short reading also conveys giving, as in Arabic expressions for bringing error or correctness; it ultimately means the same as the long reading.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r13.anchor: ومجيئوهم ذلك على وجه الإعطاء كما تقول: أتيت خطئا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r14.speaker: أهل المدينة ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r14.claim: The Medinese and Yaʿqub read with second-person ta and a jussive form: so that you yourselves increase through other people’s wealth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r14.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة، ويعقوب: "لتربوا" بالتاء وضمها وسكون الواو على الخطاب، أي: لتربوا أنتم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r15.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r15.claim: Other readers use third-person ya with an accusative verb, making usury itself grow, as in the following clause.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r15.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالياء وفتحها، ونصب الواو وجعلوا الفعل للربا لقوله: {فلا يربو عند الله}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r16.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r16.claim: Here growth in people’s wealth is described as usury’s seizing and drawing in their property.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p272/r16.anchor: في أموال الناس، أي: في اختطاف أموال الناس واجتذابها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وطاوس وقتادة والضحاك وأكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Tawus, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and most exegetes say this is a gift expecting greater return: permissible but unrewarded in the hereafter; they say it was forbidden to the Prophet by 74:6, understood as giving while seeking more.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r1.anchor: فقال سعيد بن جبير، ومجاهد، وطاوس، وقتادة، والضحاك، وأكثر المفسرين: هو الرجل يعطي غيره العطية ليثيب أكثر منها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r2.speaker: النخعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r2.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi says this is giving a friend or relative so that the recipient’s wealth increases, without seeking God’s face.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r2.anchor: وقال النخعي: هو الرجل يعطي صديقه أو قريبه ليكثر ماله ولا يريد به وجه الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r3.speaker: الشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says it is serving and traveling with a man and receiving profit from his wealth in return for help, rather than for God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r3.anchor: وقال الشعبي: هو الرجل يلتزق بالرجل فيخدمه ويسافر معه فيجعل له ربح ماله التماس عونه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r4.claim: Charity given seeking God’s face earns multiplied reward, ten times over; al-mudaʿifun are those with doubled good deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r4.anchor: {تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون} يضاعف لهم الثواب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r5.claim: Arabic calls a people lean or fat when their camels have become lean or fat, illustrating the form for those doubled in reward.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p273/r5.anchor: تقول العرب: القوم مهزولون ومسمونون: إذا هزلت أو سمنت إبلهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r7.claim: Ribā here is an unlawful transaction increase or a gift expecting greater compensation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r7.anchor: زيادة محرمة في المعاملة أو عطية يتوقع بها مزيد مكافأة

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r8.speaker: ابن كثير
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r8.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads ribā in the shortened form, meaning what you bring by giving an increase.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير بالقصر بمعنى ما جئتم به من إعطاء ربا

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r9.claim: The giver seeks to increase or make the recipient's wealth grow.

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r10.claim: That increase does not grow with God, become pure, or receive blessing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r10.anchor: فلا يزكو عنده ولا يبارك فيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r11.speaker: نافع ويعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r11.claim: Nāfiʿ and Yaʿqūb read li-tarbū, meaning you increase or become characterized by ribā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r11.anchor: وقرأ نافع ويعقوب «لتربوا» أي لتزيدوا أو لتصيروا

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r12.claim: Giving alms seeking God's face means seeking Him sincerely.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r12.anchor: تريدون وجه الله } تبتغون به وجهه خالصا

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r13.claim: Muḍʿifūn may mean possessors of multiplied reward or those whose reward and property charity multiplies; the form resembles words for strength or wealth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r13.anchor: ذوو الأضعاف من الثواب ونظير المضعف المقوي

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r14.claim: A reading opens the ʿayn; its departure from parallel phrasing intensifies the meaning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r14.anchor: وقرىء بفتح العين وتغييره عن سنن المقابلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r15.claim: The shift to third person exalts recipients before angels and elite creatures or generalizes the statement to anyone who does this.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r15.anchor: والالتفات فيه للتعظيم كأنه خاطب به الملائكة

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r16.claim: If mā is relative, the omitted return is al-muḍʿifūna bihi; alternatively, the ellipsis is fa-muʾtūhu ulāʾika hum al-muḍʿifūn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:38-39/r16.anchor: والراجع منه محذوف إن جعلت ما موصولة تقديره المضعفون به

BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r10.speaker: ابن كثير
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r10.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the verb without lengthening, covering giver, receiver, and intermediary; others lengthen it to mean giving.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r10.anchor: في قراءة ابن كثير بالقصر ليعم المعطي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r11.claim: Riba here is money given to obtain a larger return; Biqaʿi calls this prohibited or disliked, forbidden for the Prophet and disliked for ordinary people.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r11.anchor: مال على وجه الربا المحرم أو المكروه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r12.speaker: المدنيون ويعقوب
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r12.claim: The Madinan readers and Yaqub use the form with initial tāʾ, from arba, expressing an increase sought by the giver or recipient.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r12.anchor: على قراءة المدنيين ويعقوب بالفوقانية المضمومة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r13.claim: The increase is described as occurring in people’s wealth, hinting the usurer does not truly own what he takes from them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r13.anchor: فهو كناية عن أن الزيادة التي يأخذها المربي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r14.claim: The usurious increase does not grow or become pure with God; it is unblessed and ultimately effaced.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p628/r14.anchor: وكل ما لا يربو عند الله فهو غير مبارك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r1.claim: Biqaʿi connects usury’s failure to grow with 2:276, where God effaces usury and increases charities.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r2.claim: The long-vowel reading is agreed and means giving, avoiding any suggestion that the verse encourages taking zakat.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r2.anchor: للإجماع على مدة لئلا يوهم الترغيب في أخذ الزكاة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r3.claim: Zakat means charity, named for the purification and increase it brings to wealth, bodies, and character.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r3.anchor: وعبر عنها بذلك ليفيد الطهارة والزيادة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r4.claim: The giver seeks God alone with full awareness of His majesty, greatness, and perfection.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r5.claim: Face stands for God’s essence because it evokes reverence and modesty when seen and is the noblest part of the person.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r5.anchor: وعبر عن الذات بالوجه لأنه الذي يجل صاحبه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r6.claim: The singular address encourages giving by treating the Prophet as the one who fully understands its merit.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r6.anchor: ولعل إفراد المخاطب هنا للترغيب في الإيتاء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r7.claim: The distant demonstrative honors the rare, distinguished givers among the many addressed.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r7.anchor: وبالإشارة إليه بأداة البعد إعلامكا بعلو رتبته

BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r8.claim: The sincere giver’s wealth is multiplied in this life through protection and blessing and in the next through reward from tenfold to beyond measure.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r8.anchor: أي الذين ضاعفوا أموالهم في الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r9.claim: The form describes those possessing multiplied increase, like words for someone possessing strength, wealth, fatness, or thirst.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p629/r9.anchor: كما يقال : مقو وموسر ومسمن معطش

DURR-FULL:v6p495/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes two kinds of increase: one is unobjectionable, namely a gift given in hope of receiving more, while another is impermissible.
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وما آتيتم من ربا} قال: الربا رباآن ربا لا بأس به وربا لا يصلح

DURR-FULL:v6p495/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains this increase as a gift given by one person to another in expectation of a larger return.
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {وما آتيتم من ربا}

DURR-FULL:v6p495/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies the increase as gifts, or property given in hope of getting something better back.
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس فلا يربو عند الله} قال: هي الهدايا

DURR-FULL:v6p495/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r6.claim: Mujahid also describes giving one’s property while seeking a better return from its recipient.
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس فلا يربو عند الله} قال: يعطي ما له يبتغي أفضل منه

DURR-FULL:v6p495/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r7.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says a gift given to be repaid in this world earns no reward with God.
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه {وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس فلا يربو عند الله} قال: ما أعطيتم من عطية لتثابوا عليها في الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v6p495/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r8.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak calls this permissible increase: a gift given to obtain more brings neither reward nor sin, and says the Prophet specifically forbade giving in order to receive more, connecting it to 73:6.
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه في قوله {وما آتيتم من ربا} قال: هو الربا الحلال أن تهدي أكثر منه وليس له أجر ولا وزر

DURR-FULL:v6p495/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r9.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r9.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab contrasts a gift intended to earn repayment plus an increase, which does not grow with God, with giving purely for God without seeking any return, which God multiplies.
DURR-FULL:v6p495/r9.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي رضي الله عنه {وما آتيتم من ربا} قال: الرجل يعطي الشيء ليكافئه به ويزداد عليه {فلا يربو عند الله}

DURR-FULL:v6p496/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p496/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p496/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the zakat mentioned here means charity.
DURR-FULL:v6p496/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وما آتيتم من زكاة} قال: هي الصدقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p104/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p104/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p104/r5.claim: After urging support for needy kin and the resulting success, the passage discourages usury, common in pre-Islamic and early Islamic times especially among Thaqīf and Quraysh; exploiting a needy borrower contradicts mutual aid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p104/r5.anchor: لما جرى الترغيب والأمر ببذل المال لذوي الحاجة وصلة الرحم وما في ذلك من الفلاح أعقب بالتزهيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r1.claim: Mā is a general conditional, and the sentence is an inserted qualification after the preceding command; it warns of blameworthy giving and addresses God-seeking Muslims who used to lend at interest before its prohibition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r1.anchor: و { ما } شرطية تفيد العموم ، فالجملة معترضة بعد جملة { فئاتت ذا القربى حقه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r2.claim: “You gave” means some of you gave to others, since giving entails both a donor and a recipient.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r2.anchor: ومعنى { ءاتيتم : } آتى بعضكم بعضا لأن الإيتاء يقتضي معطيا وآخذا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r3.claim: The address in “so that it may increase” is directed to the party receiving the usurious gain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r3.anchor: وقوله { لتربوا في أموال الناس } خطاب للفريق الآخذ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r4.claim: Tarbu means to increase your own wealth; fī is figurative for “from,” so the profits are gained from other people’s assets.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r4.anchor: و { لتربوا } لتزيدوا ، أي لأنفسكم أموالا على أموالكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r5.claim: The poet Sabr al-Faqʿasī uses fī in the sense “from” in “we drink and gamble from their prices”; the same usage occurs in “provide for them therein and clothe them” at 4:5.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r5.anchor: قول سبرة الفقعسي : ونشرب في أثمانها ونقامر أي نشرب ونقامر من أثمان إبلنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r6.claim: Min in both “from usury” and “from alms” explains the ambiguity of the two instances of general mā; usury was discussed earlier in al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p105/r6.anchor: ومن } في قوله { من ربا } وقوله { من زكاة } بيانية مبينة لإبهام { ما } الشرطية في الموضعين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r1.claim: The conditional answer means the interest does not grow in God’s estimation: it is deficient and blameworthy; this reading keeps ribā in its familiar sense and fits 2:276, the doubled language here, and 3:130.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r1.anchor: ومعنى { فلا يربو عند الله } أنه عمل ناقص عند الله غير زاكك عنده ، والنقص يكنى به عن المذمة والتحقير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r2.speaker: السدي والحسن
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r2.claim: Al-Suddī and al-Ḥasan transmit the interpretation that the usurious gain is deficient and blameworthy with God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r2.anchor: وهذا المعنى مروي عن السدي والحسن . وقد استقام بتوجيهه المعنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r3.speaker: جم غفير من المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r3.claim: Many commentators take ribā to mean a gift to wealthy people meant to increase their favor or holdings, including reciprocal, ingratiating, or flattering gifts; the aim is to show such giving earns no divine approval.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r3.anchor: ودرج على هذا المعنى جم غفير من المفسرين فيصير المعنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r4.claim: On the alternative gift reading, “so that you increase” restates the intended increase and thereby attaches the phrase to “in people’s wealth.”

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r5.claim: The clause about alms returns to the preceding command to give the relative his due, since that right is called zakat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r5.anchor: رجوع إلى قوله { فئاتت ذا القربى حقه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r6.claim: The final clause answers the alms condition: its givers are those whose reward is multiplied; the separating pronoun restricts that title rhetorically to them, disregarding transient worldly gains, and the demonstrative honors them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r6.anchor: وجملة { فأولئك هم المضعفون } جواب { وما ءاتيتم من زكاة ، } أي فمؤتوه المضعفون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r7.claim: The increase is multiplied reward, and the demonstrative in place of a pronoun honors those who give alms for God’s sake.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p106/r7.anchor: وهو إضعاف الثواب . وضمير الفصل لقصر جنس المضعفين على هؤلاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r1.claim: Most readers pronounce ءاتيتم with two hamzas, meaning ‘you gave’; Ibn ʿĀshūr records this reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { ءاتيتم } بهمزتين ، أي أعطيتم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads أتيتم with one hamza, meaning ‘you intended’ or ‘did’.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r2.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير { أتيتم } بهمزة واحدة ، أي قصدتم ، أي فعلتم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r3.claim: Most readers pronounce ليربو with an open yāʾ and nominative final vowel on the wāw.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { ليربو } بتحتية مفتوحة وفتحة إعراب على واو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r4.speaker: نافع
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ reads لتربوا with addressed tāʾ, ḍamma, and a quiescent plural wāw.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع { لتربوا } بتاء الخطاب مضمومة وواو ساكنة هي واو الجماعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r5.claim: The muṣḥaf writes an alif after the wāw; by agreement this is not a plural marker, and the written form is authoritative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r5.anchor: وكتب في المصاحف بألف بعد الواو وليس واو جماعة بالاتفاق ، ورسم المصحف سنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r6.claim: This second resumption among four proofs establishes God’s exclusive control and refutes divine partners, while also adducing resurrection, as in Yūnus 10:34.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p107/r6.anchor: هذا الاستئناف الثاني من الأربعة التي أقيمت عليها دلائل انفراد الله تعالى بالتصرف في الناس وإبطال ما زعموه من الإشراك

BURSEVI:v7p31/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p31/r1.claim: The written wāw in ribā either marks an emphatic spelling like ṣalāh and zakāh, or recalls its root rabā-yarbū, to increase.
BURSEVI:v7p31/r1.anchor: كتب بالواو للتفخيم على لغة من يفخم في أمثاله من الصلوة والزكوة أو للتنبيه على أصله لأنه من ربا يربو زاد

BURSEVI:v7p31/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p31/r2.claim: Ribā is an uncompensated increase in an exchange: excess of the same kind in food or currency is ribā al-faḍl, while deferred exchange is ribā al-nasāʾ; both are forbidden.
BURSEVI:v7p31/r2.anchor: وهي الزيادة في المقدار بأن يباع أحد مطعوم أو نقد بنقد بأكثر منه من جنسه ويقال له ربا الفضل أو في الأجل

BURSEVI:v7p31/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p31/r3.claim: An increase taken without countervalue may grow in other people’s wealth but does not increase or receive blessing with God; God says He erases usury.
BURSEVI:v7p31/r3.anchor: لا يزيد عنده ولا يبارك له فيه

BURSEVI:v7p31/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v7p31/r4.claim: Some interpret ribā here as a gift given in expectation of a better return: it is permissible, but earns no afterlife reward without seeking God’s face; it was forbidden to the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v7p31/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : المراد بالربا في الآية هو أن يعطي الرجل العطية

BURSEVI:v7p31/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p31/r5.claim: Calling a loan a gift or waiving the claim does not make a transaction God forbade lawful or stop it being ribā.
BURSEVI:v7p31/r5.anchor: لو قال المعطي للآخذ أنا لا أعطي هذا المال إياك على أنه ربا وجعله في حل لا يكون حلالا ولا يخرج عن كونه ربا

BURSEVI:v7p31/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p31/r6.claim: Giver and receiver share the warning, except where the giver faces compelling necessity and can find no lender without a compensating return.
BURSEVI:v7p31/r6.anchor: وإلى أن المعطي والآخذ سواء في الوعيد إلا إذا كانت الضرورة قوية في جانب المعطي فلم يجد بدا من الأخذ

BURSEVI:v7p31/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p31/r7.claim: Zakah here means either obligatory alms or charity; it is named for its growth and increase.
BURSEVI:v7p31/r7.anchor: مفروضة أو صدقة سميت زكاة لأنها تزكو وتنمو

BURSEVI:v7p31/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p31/r8.claim: Seeking God’s face means sincerely seeking His reward and pleasure, not another reward or people’s praise and reputation.
BURSEVI:v7p31/r8.anchor: تبتغون به وجهه خالصا أي : ثوابه ورضاه لا ثواب غيره

BURSEVI:v7p31/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p31/r9.claim: Al-muḍʿifūn are people granted multiplied reward, or those whose reward and wealth are multiplied through zakah’s blessing; the terms resemble words for the strong and wealthy.

BURSEVI:v7p31/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p31/r10.claim: Shifting from direct address to a report indicates that the promise applies to all accountable people until the Resurrection, not only the original addressees.
BURSEVI:v7p31/r10.anchor: فعدل عن الخطاب إلى الأخبار إيماء إلى أنه لم يخص به المخاطبون بل هو عام

BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r1.speaker: سهل
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r1.claim: Sahl says multiplication is due to intending God’s face, not merely to giving zakah.
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r1.anchor: قال سهل رحمه الله : وقع التضعيف لإرادة وجه الله به

BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r2.speaker: سهل
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r2.claim: Sahl describes bodily zakah as purification from sins and monetary zakah as purification from doubtful matters.
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r2.anchor: وزكاة البدن في تطهيره من المعاصي وزكاة المال في تطهيره من الشبهات

BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r3.claim: Spending in God’s path purifies the self from worldly love; the Taʾwīlāt gives Abu Bakr as an example of giving wealth to purify himself.
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r3.anchor: يشير إلى أن في إنفاق المال في سبيل الله تزكية النفس عن لوث حب الدنيا كما كان حال أبي بكر

BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r4.claim: The cited verses portray Abu Bakr giving to purify himself, with no favor to repay and solely seeking his Lord’s highest face—out of longing to meet Him.

BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r5.claim: The sincere receive multiples beyond their hopes: their expectations are limited by present perspective, while God gives from timeless generosity without end.
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r5.anchor: يعطون أضعاف ما يرجون ويتمنون لأنهم بقدر هممهم وحسب نظرهم المحدث يرجون والله تعالى بحسب إحسانه وكرمه القديم يعطي عطاء غير منقطع

BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r6.claim: Wealth is a recoverable loan in a person’s hand; only a fool would fail to save himself from lasting punishment with what will not remain his.
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r6.anchor: واعلم أن المال عارية مستردة في يد الإنسان ولا أحد أجهل ممن لا ينقذ نفسه من العذاب الدائم بما لا يبقى في يده

BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r7.claim: God guarantees compensation for what is spent; the Mathnawi depicts angels asking God to replenish spenders and bring loss upon misers.
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r7.anchor: كفت يغمبركه دائم بهر ند دو فرشته خوش منادى ميكند

BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r8.claim: The Bustan poem urges giving now, carrying provision forward, consoling the needy, and welcoming petitioners before one’s own day of need.
BURSEVI:v7p31#2/r8.anchor: ريشان كن امروز كنجينه ست كه فردا كليدش نه در دست تست

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r1.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r1.claim: The majority read ātaytum with a long ā, meaning “what you give.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r1.anchor: قرأ جمهور القراء «وما آتيتم» بمعنى وما أعطيتم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads without length, meaning “what you do,” as in saying “I did right” or “I did wrong.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير «ما أتيتم» بغير مد بمعنى ما فعلتم كما تقول أتيت صوابا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r3.speaker: القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r3.claim: All readers agree on the long form of ātaytum in the clause about alms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r3.anchor: وأجمعوا على المد في قوله وما آتيتم من زكاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير وطاوس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr, and Ṭāwūs say the verse concerns gifts given in expectation of a return; related transactions may be lawful but earn no reward or increase with God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r5.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وابن جبير وطاوس: هذه آية نزلت في هبات الثواب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وإبراهيم النخعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī say the verse concerns gifts to relatives and brothers meant to benefit and enrich them; Ibn ʿAṭiyya sees this as close to the first interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وإبراهيم النخعي: نزلت في قوم يعطون قراباتهم وإخوانهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r7.speaker: الشعبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says worldly service performed to gain a benefit does not grow with God; Ibn ʿAṭiyya also places this near the first interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r7.anchor: وقال الشعبي: معنى الآية أن ما خدم الإنسان به أحدا وخف به لينتفع في دنياه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya also sees a possible prohibition of commercial usury: it brings sin and loss of blessing, while sincere almsgiving earns multiplied recompense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون معنى هذه الآية النهي عن الربا في التجارات لما حض عز وجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r9.claim: Usury aimed at increasing wealth from other people does not grow or become pure with God and entails sin and loss of blessing; alms given for God are repaid many times over.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r9.anchor: فإن ذلك «لا يربوا عند الله» ولا يزكو بل يتعلق فيه الإثم ومحق البركة، وما أعطى الإنسان من زكاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r10.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r10.claim: Al-Suddī says the verse was revealed about Thaqīf’s usury, which Quraysh also practiced with them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r10.anchor: وقال السدي: نزلت هذه الآية في ربا ثقيف لأنهم كانوا يعملون بالربا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r11.speaker: جمهور القراء السبعة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r11.claim: The majority of the seven readers use liyarbū, making ribā the subject of the verb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r11.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء السبعة «ليربو» بالياء وإسناد الفعل إلى الربا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r12.speaker: نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r12.claim: Nāfiʿ reads liturbū with ḍamma on the tāʾ, “so that you may increase”; Ibn ʿAbbās, Medinese readers, al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, Abū Rajāʾ, and al-Shaʿbī are also reported to read it this way, and Abū Ḥātim calls it his reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r12.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحده «لتربوا» بضم التاء على وزن تفعلوا بمعنى تكونوا ذوي زيادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r13.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r13.claim: Abū Mālik reads the verb with a feminine object pronoun: liturbūhā.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r14.claim: Al-muḍʿif has multiplied rewards, like al-muʾallaf has thousands; the form is common, as in akhṣaba for one with abundant growth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p339/r14.anchor: و «المضعف» الذي هو ذو أضعاف من الثواب كما المؤلف الذي له آلاف،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والضحاك، وقتادة، وعكرمة، ومحمد بن كعب، والشعبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r3.claim: These authorities explain this riba as a gift given in hope that recipients will return more; it earns no reward with God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r3.anchor: أي: من أعطى عطية يريد أن يرد الناس عليه أكثر مما أهدى لهم، فهذا لا ثواب له عند الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r4.claim: This exchange-seeking gift is permissible though unrewarded, but the Prophet specifically forbade it, as al-Dahhak understands the prohibition against giving in expectation of more.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r4.anchor: وهذا الصنيع مباح (4) وإن كان لا ثواب فيه (5) إلا أنه قد نهى عنه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خاصة، قاله الضحاك، واستدل بقوله: {ولا تمنن تستكثر} [المدثر: 6]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas distinguishes two kinds of riba: invalid sale riba and a permissible gift made in hope of receiving extra.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الربا رباءان، فربا لا يصح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r6.claim: Reward with God is instead for zakat given seeking His face, for which He multiplies the reward and recompense.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r6.anchor: وإنما الثواب عند الله في الزكاة؛ ولهذا قال: {وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون} أي: الذين يضاعف الله لهم الثواب والجزاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r7.claim: A sound hadith says God receives charity equal to a date from lawful earnings and nurtures it for its giver until it becomes greater than Mount Uhud.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p318#2/r7.anchor: كما [جاء] (8) في الصحيح: "وما تصدق أحد بعدل تمرة من كسب طيب إلا أخذها الرحمن بيمينه، فيربيها لصاحبها كما يربي أحدكم فلوه أو فصيله، حتى تصير التمرة أعظم من أحد" (9) .

JISHUMI:v8p5623/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir reads أتيتم with a short initial alif; the other readers use آتيتم, meaning “you gave.”
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير: (أتيتم) مقصورة الألف غير ممدودة، وقرأ الباقون: (آتيتم) ممدودة بالألف بمعنى أعطيتم

JISHUMI:v8p5623/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع ويعقوب وابن عباس والحسن وأبو حاتم
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r2.claim: These authorities read لتربوا with tāʾ and a silent wāw, addressing the recipients as the ones who seek increase; Abu Hatim prefers this parsing.
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع ويعقوب: لتربوا بالتاء وضمها وسكون الواو، وهو قراءة ابن عباس والحسن، واختيار أبي حاتم على الخطاب

JISHUMI:v8p5623/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r3.speaker: الباقون وأبو عبيد
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r3.claim: The other readers use يربو, with the increase attributed to usury itself; Abu Ubayd prefers this in view of the following فلا يربو عند الله.
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: (ليربو) بالياء وفتحها ونصب الواو وجعل الفعل مضافا إلى الربا، واختاره أبو عبيد لقوله: (فلا يربو عند الله)

JISHUMI:v8p5623/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r6.claim: In Arabic ribā means increase; in law it names an invalid contract even when there is no increase, such as deferred gold-for-gold exchange.
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r6.anchor: والربا في اللغة: الزيادة، وهو في الشرع اسم لعقد فاسد، وإن لم يكن فيه زيادة كبيع الذهب بالذهب نساء

JISHUMI:v8p5623/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r7.claim: Ḍiʿf is a like amount or double; muḍʿif is one possessing multiples, just as mūsir is one possessing wealth.
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r7.anchor: وضعف الشيء: مثله، والمضعف ذو الأضعاف، كما أن الموسر ذو اليسار

JISHUMI:v8p5623/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r8.claim: A report says the clause about usury was revealed concerning Thaqif, who practiced usury.
JISHUMI:v8p5623/r8.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: (وما آتيتم من ربا) في ثقيف كانوا يربون

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say this is a gift given in hope of receiving a larger return.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r7.anchor: أحدها : أنه الرجل يهدي هدية ليكافأ عليها أفضل منها , قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r8.speaker: الشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r8.claim: Al-Sha'bi says this describes a traveler serving someone who then gives him part of his profit as payment, without seeking God’s pleasure.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r8.anchor: الثاني : أنه في رجل صحبه في الطريق فخدمه فجعل له المخدوم بعض الربح من ماله جزاء لخدمته لا لوجه الله , قاله الشعبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r9.speaker: إبراهيم
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r9.claim: Ibrahim says this is money given to a relative to make the recipient wealthier, without seeking reward from God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r9.anchor: الثالث : أنه في رجل يهب لذي قرابة له مالا ليصير به غنيا ذا مال ولا يفعله طلبا لثواب الله , قاله إبراهيم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r10.claim: The gift does not grow with God because it earns no reward from Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r10.anchor: أي فلا يكون له ثواب عند الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says there are two kinds of riba, one lawful and one unlawful; what people exchange among themselves is lawful but does not reach God as a reward.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هما ربوان أحدهما حلال والآخر حرام

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r12.claim: Seeking God’s face means seeking His reward; the apparent interpretation is the obligatory zakat.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r12.anchor: أي ثواب الله , وفيها قولان : أحدهما : أنها الزكاة المفروضة وهو الظاهر

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r13.claim: Another interpretation, reported from Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi, takes zakat here as voluntary charity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r13.anchor: الثاني : أنها الصدقة , قاله ابن عباس والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r14.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r14.claim: Al-Suddi says their good deeds are multiplied, since a good deed earns tenfold.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r14.anchor: أحدهما : تضاعف لهم الحسنات لأن من جاء بالحسنة فله عشر أمثالها , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r15.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r15.claim: The second view says their wealth increases in this world; al-Kalbi adds that zakat does not diminish anyone’s wealth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p315/r15.anchor: الثاني : تضاعف أموالهم في الدنيا بالزيادة فيها , وقال الكلبي : لم يقل مال رجل من زكاة

MUJAHID:v2p501/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p501/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p501/r1.claim: Mujahid explains this as giving a gift in hope of receiving something better in return; it earns no reward with God.
MUJAHID:v2p501/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ فلا يربو عند الله ﴾ يعني من أعطى هدية يبتغي أفضل منها فلا أجر فيها

MUQATIL:30:37-40/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:30:37-40/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:30:37-40/r6.claim: The passage was revealed concerning people among the Prophet's Companions who engaged in gambling; it describes a gift given in hopes of getting more from others.
MUQATIL:30:37-40/r6.anchor: نزلت في أهل الميسر من أصحاب النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم، يقول: أعطيتم من عطية ليلتمس بها الزيادة من الناس،

MUQATIL:30:37-40/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:30:37-40/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:30:37-40/r7.claim: Such a gift is neither multiplied nor purified with God, though there is no sin in it.
MUQATIL:30:37-40/r7.anchor: فلا يربو عند الله } يقول: فلا تضاعف تلك العطية عند الله، ولا تزكوا، ولا إثم فيه،

MUQATIL:30:37-40/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:30:37-40/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:30:37-40/r8.claim: A charitable gift intended for God's sake is the kind of giving that God multiplies.
MUQATIL:30:37-40/r8.anchor: ومآ آتيتم من زكاة } يقول: وما أعطيتم من صدقة { تريدون } بها { وجه الله } ففيه الأضعاف،

MUQATIL:30:37-40/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:30:37-40/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:30:37-40/r9.claim: The multiplied reward begins at tenfold and goes beyond that.
MUQATIL:30:37-40/r9.anchor: فأولئك هم المضعفون } [آية: 39] الواحدة عشرة فصاعدا.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r1.claim: The phrase means giving the interest gained by usury so recipients' wealth grows; it does not grow or become blessed with God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r1.anchor: يريد وما أعطيتم أكله الربا من ربا ليربوا فى أموالهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r2.claim: Another view takes this as lawful riba: a gift given in expectation of receiving more, which has no increase with God because it does not seek Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r2.anchor: وقيل هو من الربا الحلال أى وما تعطونه من الهدية لتأخذوا أكثر منها فلا يربوا عند الله لأنكم لم تريدوا بذلك وجه الله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r3.claim: Meccan readers recite ataytum without a long vowel on the initial hamza.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r3.anchor: أتيتم من ربا بلا مد مكى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r4.speaker: المدنيون
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r4.claim: The Medinan reading uses ta in the verb, meaning so that you increase their wealth.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r4.anchor: لتربوا مدنى أى لتزيدوا فى أموالهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r5.claim: Zakat means charity given sincerely for God, without seeking repayment, ostentation, or reputation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r5.anchor: تبتغون به وجهه خالصا لا تطلبون به مكافأة ولا رياء ولاسمعة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r6.claim: Al-mudʿifun are people given multiplied rewards; the phrase implies a pronoun referring back to the relative expression.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r6.anchor: ذوو الأضعاف من الحسنات ونظير المضعف المقوى والموسر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r7.claim: The shift to third person is an apt iltifat that generalizes the point to anyone who acts this way.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r7.anchor: التفات حسن لأنه يفيد التعميم كأنه قيل من فعل هذا فسبيله سبيل المخاطبين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r8.speaker: الزجاج
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the phrase as recipients receiving ten times the reward for each good deed.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p275/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج فى قوله فأولئك هم المضعفون أى فأهلها هم المضعفون أى هم الذين يضاعف لهم الثواب يعطون بالحسنة عشر امثالها

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r1.claim: After mentioning what is done seeking God’s pleasure and reward, the passage turns to another kind of giving and then returns to what is sought for Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r1.anchor: لما ذكر ما يراد به وجهه ويثيب عليه ذكر غير ذلك من الصفة وما يراد به أيضا وجهه

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r2.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r2.claim: The majority read ātaytum with a long vowel, meaning ‘you gave.’

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r3.speaker: ابن كثير ومجاهد وحميد
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir, Mujahid, and Humayd read without lengthening, meaning what you do of usury so it may increase.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ومجاهد وحميد بغير مد بمعنى ما فعلتم من ربا ليربو

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r4.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r4.claim: All readers agree on the lengthened reading in the second phrase.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r4.anchor: وأجمعوا على المد في قوله: { ومآ آتيتم من ربا

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r5.claim: Ribā means increase; the author contrasts forbidden usury discussed in al-Baqara with the permissible kind here, concluding there are lawful and unlawful forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r5.anchor: والربا الزيادة وقد مضى في «البقرة» معناه

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r6.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r6.claim: Ikrima says ribā has a lawful and a forbidden kind; the lawful kind is a gift given in hope of receiving something better.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r6.anchor: قال عكرمة في قوله تعالى: { ومآ آتيتم من ربا

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r7.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the phrase with a lawful gift made in hope of a better return; it earns neither reward nor sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r7.anchor: وعن الضحاك في هذه الآية: هو الربا الحلال الذي يهدى

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says it means a gift offered in hope of a better return: its giver is not rewarded by God but is not sinful.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r8.anchor: وكذلك قال ابن عباس: «وما آتيتم من ربا» يريد هدية الرجل

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير وطاوس ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Tawus, and Mujahid say the verse was revealed about gifts given expecting compensation.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس وابن جبير وطاوس ومجاهد: هذه آية نزلت في هبة الثواب

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya extends the point to acts such as greeting someone to obtain repayment: they incur no sin but earn no reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r10.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وما جرى مجراها مما يصنعه الإنسان ليجازى عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r11.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r11.claim: Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi also adopts the view that such an act earns neither sin nor reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r11.anchor: لا أجر فيه ولا زيادة عند الله تعالى. وقاله القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r12.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن علقمة
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r12.claim: Al-Nasaʾi reports that the Thaqif delegation brought the Prophet a gift; he asked whether it was charity or a gift, explained the intentions, and accepted it as a gift.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r12.anchor: وفي كتاب النسائي عن عبد الرحمن بن علقمة قال

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r13.speaker: ابن عباس وإبراهيم النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi say the verse concerns people who support relatives or brothers so they can benefit and grow wealthier.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وإبراهيم النخعي: نزلت في قوم يعطون قراباتهم وإخوانهم
