QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r14.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r14.claim: Al-Shaʿbi explains it as serving someone lightly to gain worldly benefit; the service repaid in this life does not grow with God.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r14.anchor: وقال الشعبي: معنى الآية أن ما خدم الإنسان به أحدا وخف له

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r15.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r15.claim: One view says the ban on giving to receive more applied specifically to the Prophet, citing the command not to give expecting an increase.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39/r15.anchor: وقيل: كان هذا حراما على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الخصوص

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r1.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r1.claim: Another view identifies the phrase with forbidden usury and says the taker cannot claim it as his; it belongs to the person from whom it was taken.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: إنه الربا المحرم فمعنى: «لا يربو عند الله» على هذا القول لا يحكم به لآخذه بل هو للمأخوذ منه.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r2.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse was revealed about usury practiced by Thaqif and by Quraysh against them.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r2.anchor: قال السدي: نزلت هذه الآية في ربا ثقيف لأنهم كانوا يعملون بالربا وتعمله فيهم قريش.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the verse expressly concerns someone who gives a gift seeking an increase from other people in return.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r3.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي: صريح الآية فيمن يهب

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r4.claim: The author says Ali's threefold classification of gifts is correct.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r4.anchor: الثالثة: ما ذكره علي رضي الله عنه وفصله من الهبة صحيح

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r5.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r5.claim: Malik allows recompense when the giver is someone who normally expects it from the recipient, such as a poor person giving to a rich person; this is one Shafiʿi position.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r5.anchor: فقال مالك: ينظر فيه فإن كان مثله ممن يطلب

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa and Shafiʿi's other position deny recompense without a condition; a gift for return is invalid because it resembles a sale for an unknown price.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: لا يكون له ثواب إذا لم يشترط

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r7.speaker: الكوفي
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r7.claim: The Kufan argument is that imposing compensation destroys the gratuitous nature of a gift and turns it into an exchange.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r7.anchor: واحتج الكوفي بأن موضوع الهبة التبرع

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r8.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r8.claim: In Malik's Muwatta, Umar says a gift given with expectation of return remains the giver's until he is satisfied with the return.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r8.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أنه قال: أيما رجل وهب

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r9.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r9.claim: Ali classifies gifts as intended for God, for people, or for recompense; the giver may reclaim the third kind if no recompense is given.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r9.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: المواهب ثلاث

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r10.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r10.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet accepted gifts and repaid them; he did not condemn a giver for seeking recompense, only resentment at a return above value.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#2/r10.anchor: باب المكافأة في الهبة وساق حديث عائشة قالت

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r1.claim: The Prophet taught that deeds are judged by intentions and each person receives according to what he intended.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r1.anchor: الأعمال بالنيات وإنما لكل امرىء ما نوى

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r2.claim: A gift intended for God's pleasure earns reward through His grace and mercy, as the verse promises multiplied reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r2.anchor: فأما إذا أراد بهبته وجه الله تعالى وابتغى عليه الثواب من عنده

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r3.claim: Supporting a relative so they are not left dependent is judged by intention: worldly display is not for God, while fulfilling kinship rights is.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r3.anchor: وكذلك من يصل قرابته ليكون غنيا حتى لا يكون كلا

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r4.claim: A gift made to win people's praise has no benefit or reward; the author links this to the warning against ostentatious charity.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r4.anchor: وأما من أراد بهبته وجوه الناس رياء ليحمدوه عليها

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r5.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r5.claim: For a gift given expecting recompense, Ibn al-Qasim allows revocation until the recipient has repaid its value.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r5.anchor: ما لم يثب بقيمتها، على مذهب ابن القاسم

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r6.speaker: عمر وعلي
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r6.claim: On the apparent sense of Umar and Ali's statements, the giver may revoke until satisfied with a return greater than the gift's value.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r6.anchor: أو ما لم يرض منها بأزيد من قيمتها، على ظاهر قول عمر وعلي

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r7.speaker: مطرف
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r7.claim: Mutarrif's position in al-Wadihah permits revocation while the donated item remains, even if its value changed or the recipient gave more than its worth.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r7.anchor: وهو قول مطرف في الواضحة: أن الهبة ما كانت

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r8.claim: Another view says that if the original gift remains unchanged, the giver may take whatever return he wants.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r8.anchor: وقد قيل: إنها إذا كانت قائمة العين لم تتغير

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r9.claim: A further opinion requires the gift's value, comparing the case to a marriage in which the dowry was not stipulated.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r10.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r10.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says that once the gift is no longer extant, only its value is owed, by agreement.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r10.anchor: ليس له إلا القيمة اتفاقا قاله ابن العربي

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r11.speaker: جمهور القراء السبعة
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r11.claim: Most of the seven readers read li-yarbu with yāʾ, making the verb refer to ribā.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r11.anchor: قرأ جمهور القراء السبعة: «ليربو» بالياء وإسناد الفعل إلى الربا

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r12.speaker: نافع وابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r12.claim: Nafiʿ alone reads with tāʾ and a still wāw, addressing the plural as becoming people of increase; Ibn Abbas, Hasan, Qatada, and al-Shaʿbi also read it this way.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r12.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحده: بضم التاء والواو ساكنة على المخاطبة بمعنى تكونوا ذوي زيادات، وهذه قراءة ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والشعبي.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r13.speaker: أبو مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r13.claim: Abu Malik reads liturbbūhā, with a feminine object pronoun.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r14.claim: This giving does not grow in purity or earn reward with God, who accepts only what is sincerely intended for Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r14.anchor: فلا يربوا عند الله } أي لا يزكوا ولا يثيب عليه لأنه لا يقبل

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses zakāh here as charity.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r15.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي من صدقة

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r16.claim: God accepts charity given for His pleasure and multiplies its reward tenfold or more, as in the cited verse about lending God a good loan.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#3/r16.anchor: أي ذلك الذي يقبله ويضاعفه له عشرة أضعافه أو أكثر

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r1.claim: The author also connects sincere spending for God's pleasure to the parable of a garden on a height.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r1.anchor: ومثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله وتثبيتا من أنفسهم

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r2.claim: The wording shifts from direct address to third person, as in the verse about being at sea and the ships moving with them.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r2.anchor: لأنه رجع من المخاطبة إلى الغيبة

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r3.claim: One explanation is that their good deeds are multiplied; another is that they possess multiplied good and bliss.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r3.anchor: وفي معنى المضعفين قولان: أحدهما: أنه تضاعف لهم الحسنات

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r4.claim: Muqwin, musmin, and muʿaṭṭash describe someone whose camels are strong, fat, or thirsty; muḍʿaf can likewise describe one whose camels are weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r4.anchor: كما يقال: فلان مقو إذا كانت إبله قوية

QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r5.claim: The commentary uses the prophetic supplication's form mukhbith for one afflicted by impurity, contrasting one bad in himself with one whose companions are bad.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:39#4/r5.anchor: فالمخبث: الذي أصابه خبث، يقال: فلان رديء أي هو رديء في نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r1.claim: The verse exhorts people: they are attracted to giving one unit expecting two, but that gift does not grow with God, whereas zakat grows with Him, so they should give zakat more readily.
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r1.anchor: ذكر هذا تحريضا يعني أنكم إذا طلب منكم واحد باثنين ترغبون فيه وتؤتونه وذلك لا يربوا عند الله والزكاة تنمو عند الله

RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r2.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r2.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that charity is placed in the Merciful’s hand and grows until it is like a mountain.
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r2.anchor: كما أخبر النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( إن الصدقة تقع في يد الرحمن فتربوا حتى تصير مثل الجبل )

RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r3.claim: The multiplied reward is at least tenfold; the multiplication concerns the good and reward of the act, not a literal tenfold quantity of the object given.
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r3.anchor: وأقل ذلك عشرة أضعاف كل مثل لما آتى في كونه حسنة لا في المقدار فلا يفهم أن من أعطى رغيفا يعطيه الله عشرة أرغفة

RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r4.claim: A single loaf can earn a heavenly palace through mercy and ten like it through grace; the difference reflects generosity beyond the action’s ordinary worth.
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r4.anchor: فبالرغيف الواحد يكون له قصر في الجنة فيه من كل شيء ثوابا

RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r5.claim: A king who ordinarily rewards a one-dirham gift with a thousand shows generosity by giving ten thousand; this illustrates divine multiplication beyond ordinary compensation.
RAZI-FULL:v25p111#2/r5.anchor: مثاله في الشاهد ، ملك عظيم قبل من عبده هدية قيمتها درهم لو عوضه بعشرة دراهم لا يكون كرما

STUDYQURAN:30:39/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r1.claim: This is the Quran's earliest chronological mention of ribā; the final-revelation verses on it are ambiguous and have fueled centuries of debate over its definition.
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r1.anchor: This is the earliest mention of usury

STUDYQURAN:30:39/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r2.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r2.claim: In this context, ribā may mean forbidden usury.
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r2.anchor: ribā is understood as a reference to either usury, which is forbidden

STUDYQURAN:30:39/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r3.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r3.claim: Ṭs also allows ribā to mean seeking increase, which is permissible.
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r3.anchor: or the seeking of increase, which is permissible (Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:30:39/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r4.claim: Q says giving someone a gift in hopes of receiving a greater return is permissible, though it brings no increase with God because deeds are rewarded according to intentions.
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r4.anchor: It is permissible to present a gift to another in the hopes of receiving something greater than it from that person

STUDYQURAN:30:39/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r5.claim: The manifold increase from alms contrasts with pre-Islamic loans whose compounding could ruin borrowers.
STUDYQURAN:30:39/r5.anchor: loans could compound exponentially, to the point of leaving the borrower in complete ruin

QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r3.claim: Give zakat for God’s sake without using the poor recipient to secure his service; charity to a hostile relative is best because it strips away personal gain.
QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r3.anchor: وألا تستخدم الفقير لما تبره به من رافقه ، بل أفضل الصدقة على ذي رحم كاشح حتى يكون إعطاؤه لله مجردا

QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r4.claim: Those who give this way multiply their reward by mastering the self against its preference and gaining recompense from God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r4.anchor: فهؤلاء هم الذين يضاعف أجرهم : قهرهم لأنفسهم حيث يخالفونها ، وفوزهم بالعوض من قبل الله

QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r5.claim: Zakat purifies wealth according to the revealed rules governing how it is paid and the categories and characteristics of wealth.
QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r5.anchor: ثم الزكاة هي التطهير ، وتطهير المال معلوم ببيان الشريعة في كيفية إخراج الزكاة ، وأصناف المال وأوصافه

QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r6.claim: A person must also perform the zakat of the body, heart, and innermost secret.
QUSHAYRI:v3p10/r6.anchor: وزكاة البدن وزكاة القلب وزكات السر

TAB-FULL:v18p503/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r1.claim: This is a gift given in expectation of an increased return from its recipient; it does not grow with God because the giver did not seek God's face.
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r1.anchor: وما أعطيتم أيها الناس بعضكم بعضا من عطية لتزداد في أموال الناس

TAB-FULL:v18p503/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this is a gift exchanged among people when the giver expects to receive more in return.
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس

TAB-FULL:v18p503/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr describes it as a gift one person gives another hoping for repayment with something better.
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، " {ما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس}

TAB-FULL:v18p503/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r4.claim: Mujāhid calls these gifts and also describes giving wealth in hope of receiving something better.
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس}

TAB-FULL:v18p503/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r5.claim: In another gloss, Mujāhid says the giver parts with wealth while seeking a better return.
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس}

TAB-FULL:v18p503/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r6.claim: Ibrāhīm says it is a person giving a gift while expecting a better gift in return.
TAB-FULL:v18p503/r6.anchor: عن إبراهيم، قال: «هو الرجل يهدي إلى الرجل الهدية، ليثيبه أفضل منها»

TAB-FULL:v18p505/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r1.speaker: ابن طاوس
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r1.claim: Ibn Ṭāwūs, quoting his father, describes a gift intended to earn a better return and says it brings neither reward nor sin.
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r1.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه: «هو الرجل يعطي العطية ويهدي الهدية ليثاب أفضل من ذلك، ليس فيه أجر ولا وزر»

TAB-FULL:v18p505/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r2.claim: Qatāda says this is what someone gives seeking worldly compensation and repayment from people; God neither accepts nor rewards it.
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، " {وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس فلا يربو عند الله}

TAB-FULL:v18p505/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says this is ordinary gift exchange for a greater return, unlike the Prophet-specific command not to give seeking more (74:6).
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r3.anchor: الضحاك، يقول، في قوله " {وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس}

TAB-FULL:v18p505/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r4.speaker: عامر
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r4.claim: ʿĀmir says the giver attaches himself to another, serves and travels with him, and advances some business profit to gain that person's help rather than God's reward.
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r4.anchor: عن عامر، " {وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس}

TAB-FULL:v18p505/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives the example of someone funding another person in order to increase that recipient's wealth, not for God's sake.
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " {وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس}

TAB-FULL:v18p505/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r6.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r6.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī says that in pre-Islamic times someone gave a relative money to enlarge the relative's wealth.
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r6.anchor: إبراهيم النخعي، يقول في قوله: " {وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس

TAB-FULL:v18p505/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r7.claim: Another view says this arrangement was lawful for everyone except the Prophet, for whom it was specifically restricted.
TAB-FULL:v18p505/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: ذلك للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خاصة، وأما لغيره فحلال

TAB-FULL:v18p507/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk calls this the lawful form of ribā reserved for the Prophet, while gifts seeking return remain ordinary practice for others.
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك، " {وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس فلا يربو عند الله}

TAB-FULL:v18p507/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the previously explained gift given in expectation of a greater return, judging that interpretation the most apparent meaning.
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r2.anchor: وإنما اخترنا القول الذي اخترناه في ذلك لأنه أظهر معانيه

TAB-FULL:v18p507/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r3.speaker: عامة قراء الكوفة والبصرة وبعض أهل مكة
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r3.claim: Most Kūfan and Basran readers and some Meccans read liyarbū with yāʾ, so the ribā itself grows in people's wealth.
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r3.anchor: فقرأته عامة قراء الكوفة والبصرة وبعض أهل مكة: {ليربو}

TAB-FULL:v18p507/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r4.speaker: عامة قراء أهل المدينة
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r4.claim: Most Medinan readers use the tāʾ reading litarbū, meaning that the givers themselves grow through people's wealth.
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r4.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء أهل المدينة: (لتربو)

TAB-FULL:v18p507/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī accepts both famous readings because their meanings are close: the owners grow the money, and the money grows through their action.
TAB-FULL:v18p507/r5.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندنا، أنهما قراءتان مشهورتان في قراء الأمصار مع تقارب معنييهما

TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r1.claim: Zakat here is charity given seeking God's face; those who give it receive doubled reward and recompense.
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون}

TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r2.claim: Al-muḍʿifūn are those granted multiplied reward; Arabic usage calls people musminīn or muʿaṭṭashīn when their camels become fat or thirsty.
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون}

TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says God accepts this charity and multiplies its reward tenfold or more.
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون}

TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the first kind as a gift meant to earn a better return, with no reward or sin, and the second as charity for God's face.
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قوله " {وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس فلا يربو عند الله}

TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid is reported as giving the same distinction between a return-seeking gift and charity offered for God's sake.
TAB-FULL:v18p507#2/r5.anchor: قال معمر: قال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، مثل ذلك

SULAMI:v2p125#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p125#3/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p125#3/r1.claim: The increase in reward comes from intending God’s face, not simply from giving zakat.
SULAMI:v2p125#3/r1.anchor: وقع التضعيف لإرادة وجه الله به لا لإيتاء الزكاة

SULAMI:v2p125#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p125#3/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p125#3/r2.claim: The body’s zakat is its cleansing from sins, and the wealth’s zakat is its cleansing from doubtful things.
SULAMI:v2p125#3/r2.anchor: والزكاة زكاة البدن في تطهيره من المعاصي وزكاة ماله

TABATABAI:30:37-39/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:37-39/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:37-39/r12.claim: Ribā means increase in wealth, and ليربوا points to the reason for calling it ribā.
TABATABAI:30:37-39/r12.anchor: الربا نماء المال، وقوله { ليربوا } الخ، يشير إلى وجه التسمية

TABATABAI:30:37-39/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:37-39/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:37-39/r13.claim: Money given so recipients’ wealth will grow is not given seeking God’s face, as the contrast with zakat shows; it earns no reward from God.
TABATABAI:30:37-39/r13.anchor: فالمراد أن المال الذي تؤتونه الناس ليزيد في أموالهم لا إرادة لوجه الله

TABATABAI:30:39/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:39/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:39/r1.claim: Here zakat means any charitable giving for God's sake without waste; al-muḍʿaf denotes one whose return is multiplied, whether wealth or reward.
TABATABAI:30:39/r1.anchor: المراد بالزكاة مطلق الصدقة أي إعطاء المال لوجه الله من غير تبذير

TABATABAI:30:39/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:39/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:39/r2.claim: On a Meccan dating, the contrast is a lawful gift without devotional intent versus charity given with devotional intent.
TABATABAI:30:39/r2.anchor: فالمراد بالربا والزكاة بقرينة المقابلة وما احتف بهما من الشواهد

TABATABAI:30:39/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:39/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:39/r3.claim: If the verse is Medinan, riba means prohibited usury and zakat means the obligatory alms.
TABATABAI:30:39/r3.anchor: وأما على تقدير كونها مدنية فالمراد بالربا الربا المحرم وبالزكاة هي الزكاة المفروضة

TABATABAI:30:39/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:39/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:39/r4.claim: This verse and the preceding one seem more Medinan than Meccan; the author gives no weight to alleged reports or transmitted consensus on their dating.
TABATABAI:30:39/r4.anchor: وهذه الآية والتي قبلها أشبه بالمدنيات منهما بالمكيات ولا اعتبار بما يدعى من الرواية أو الإجماع المنقول

TABATABAI:30:39/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:39/r5.speaker: عبيد الله بن عباس
TABATABAI:30:39/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet ended a sermon by identifying his family as the word of piety, path of guidance, highest example, greatest proof, and firmest bond.
TABATABAI:30:39/r5.anchor: في العيون عن عبيد الله بن عباس قال قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فينا خطيبا فقال في آخر خطبته

TABATABAI:30:39#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:39#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:30:39#2/r6.claim: Imam al-Sadiq distinguishes consumable riba—a gift expecting a better return, identified with this verse—from forbidden riba threatened with hell; parallel sources transmit the report.
TABATABAI:30:39#2/r6.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده عن إبراهيم اليماني عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال الربا رباءان ربا يؤكل وربا لا يؤكل

TABATABAI:30:39#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:39#2/r7.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABATABAI:30:39#2/r7.claim: Al-Majmaʿ attributes to Ali that prayer removes pride, zakat brings provision, fasting tests sincerity, and maintaining kinship increases numbers.
TABATABAI:30:39#2/r7.anchor: وفي المجمع في قوله تعالى { فأولئك هم المضعفون } قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام فرض الله الصلاة تنزيها عن الكبر

TABATABAI:30:27-39#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:27-39#3/r1.speaker: الزهراء
TABATABAI:30:27-39#3/r1.claim: Al-Fiqh quotes Fatima al-Zahra's sermon: faith purifies from shirk, prayer from pride, and zakat increases provision.
TABATABAI:30:27-39#3/r1.anchor: وفي الفقيه خطبة للزهراء عليها السلام وفيها ففرض الله الإيمان تطهيرا من الشرك والصلاة تنزيها عن الكبر والزكاة زيادة في الرزق

TABRISI:30:39/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:39/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads āteytum with a short alif; the others lengthen it.
TABRISI:30:39/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير { ما آتيتم من ربا } مقصورة الألف غير ممدودة

TABRISI:30:39/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:39/r2.claim: Medinese readers, Yaʿqūb, and Sahl read li-turbū with tāʾ, ḍamma, and still wāw; the rest read li-yarbū with yāʾ, fatḥa, and accusative wāw.
TABRISI:30:39/r2.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة ويعقوب وسهل لتربوا بالتاء وضمها وسكون الواو

TABRISI:30:39/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:30:39/r3.claim: Riba can be a gift offered in expectation of a larger return; it does not grow with God because the giver sought compensation, not God’s favor.
TABRISI:30:39/r3.anchor: ما آتيتم من هدية أهديتموها لتعوضوا ما هو أكثر منه

TABRISI:30:39/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:30:39/r4.claim: The long reading means “you gave”; the short reading can mean “you did” or “came to,” as ordinary usage for performing an act.
TABRISI:30:39/r4.anchor: فمن مد آتيتم فلأن المعنى أعطيتم

TABRISI:30:39/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:30:39/r5.claim: A poem, “أتيت الذي يأتي السفيه,” uses atā for doing what a fool does, illustrating how the short reading can describe an act.
TABRISI:30:39/r5.anchor: قال الشاعر: أتيت الذي يأتي السفيه

TABRISI:30:39/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:30:39/r6.claim: All readers lengthen āteytum in the zakāt phrase, as in “giving zakāt” at 21:73; ordinary usage and scripture favor the long form.
TABRISI:30:39/r6.anchor: ولم يختلفوا في مد وما آتيتم من زكوة

TABRISI:30:39/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39/r7.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:30:39/r7.claim: For li-yarbū, the subject is the previously mentioned riba, with an omitted genitive: it is meant to grow by attracting people’s wealth.
TABRISI:30:39/r7.anchor: ومن قرأ ليربو فإن فاعله الربا المذكور

TABRISI:30:39/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39/r8.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:30:39/r8.claim: The gift itself is not legally riba; the prohibited excess is what is taken above the principal. A gift seeking return is named for its intended increase.
TABRISI:30:39/r8.anchor: والمدفوع ليس في الحقيقة ربا إنما المحرم الزيادة

TABRISI:30:39#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس وطاوس
TABRISI:30:39#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ṭāwūs, and a report from Abū Jaʿfar, treat this as lawful gift-giving in hope of a larger return, without reward or sin.

TABRISI:30:39#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39#2/r13.speaker: الحسن والجبائي
TABRISI:30:39#2/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Jubbāʾī identify the riba as prohibited interest, as in 2:276.
TABRISI:30:39#2/r13.anchor: والقول الآخر: أنه الربا المحرم عن الحسن والجبائي

TABRISI:30:39#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:39#2/r14.claim: Nāfiʿ reads li-turbū; other readers read li-yarbū with different person, vowels, and inflection.
TABRISI:30:39#2/r14.anchor: وقول نافع لتربوا أي لتصيروا ذوي زيادة

TABRISI:30:39#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39#2/r15.speaker: نافع
TABRISI:30:39#2/r15.claim: Nāfiʿ’s reading means becoming possessors of increase from other people’s wealth, seeking and attracting it, as in arbā.
TABRISI:30:39#2/r15.anchor: أي تستدعونها وتجتلبونها وكأنه من أربى

TABRISI:30:39-40/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39-40/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:39-40/r1.claim: Zakat given to rightful recipients seeking God’s reward and approval, not repayment, makes its givers people whose reward is multiplied.
TABRISI:30:39-40/r1.anchor: أي وما أعطيتموه أهله على وجه الزكاة

TABRISI:30:39-40/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39-40/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:39-40/r2.claim: One explanation is people possessing multiplied good deeds, as a person may be described as possessing strength or wealth.
TABRISI:30:39-40/r2.anchor: وقيل: المضعفون ذوو الإضعاف في الحسنات

TABRISI:30:39-40/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39-40/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:39-40/r3.claim: Another explanation is increased wealth in this life and reward in the next, since God made zakat a cause of increased wealth.
TABRISI:30:39-40/r3.anchor: وقيل: هم المضعفون للمال في العاجل وللثواب في الآجل

TABRISI:30:39-40/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39-40/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:39-40/r4.claim: A Prophetic report says that charity does not diminish wealth.

TABRISI:30:39-40/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39-40/r5.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABRISI:30:39-40/r5.claim: ʿAlī says prayer cleanses arrogance, zakat brings provision, fasting tests sincerity, and kinship ties increase numbers, in a longer discourse.
TABRISI:30:39-40/r5.anchor: وقال أمير المؤمنين ع: فرض الله تعالى الصلاة تنزيها عن الكبر

TABRISI:30:39-40/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:39-40/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:39-40/r6.claim: The verse shifts from direct address to reported statement, a feature counted among forms of eloquence.
TABRISI:30:39-40/r6.anchor: وبدأ سبحانه في الآية بالخطاب ثم ثنى بالخبر

FARRA:v2p325/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p325/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p325/r1.claim: المضعفون are people entitled to multiplied reward; Arabs describe people through their camels’ states, as in مسمنين, مقويا for strong camels, and مضعفا for weak ones.
FARRA:v2p325/r1.anchor: وقوله: (هم المضعفون) أهل للمضاعفة كما تقول العرب أصبحتم مسمنين معطشين إذا عطشت إبلهم أو سمنت.

FARRA:v2p325/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p325/r2.speaker: الكسائي
FARRA:v2p325/r2.claim: Al-Kisa’i heard Arabs say أصبحت مقويا for strong camels and أصبحت مضعفا for weak camels.
FARRA:v2p325/r2.anchor: وسمع الكسائي العرب تقول: أصبحت مقويا أي إبلك قوية، وأصبحت مضعفا أي إبلك ضعاف

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r1.claim: The riba offering is intended to increase one's holdings through other people's wealth.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r1.anchor: وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس} أي ليزيدكم من أموال الناس.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains this as someone giving a gift in hope of receiving a greater return; it does not grow with God.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: "هو الرجل يهدي الشيء يريد أن يثاب أفضل منه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r3.claim: Zakāt here means alms or charity.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r3.anchor: وما آتيتم من زكاة} أي من صدقة.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r4.claim: Al-muḍʿifūn are those who receive multiplication and increase.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p342#2/r4.anchor: تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون} أي الذين يجدون التضعيف والزيادة (3) .

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r1.speaker: قتادة عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through Qatāda, says this is a gift given in hope of receiving a better return; it earns no reward with God but carries no sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r1.anchor: روى قتادة عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية قال: هي هدية الرجل يهدي الشيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r2.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies the riba here as gifts.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r3.speaker: ابن أبي رواد عن مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r3.claim: Mujāhid, as reported by Ibn Abī Rawwād, calls it lawful riba: a gift offered to elicit a better gift, with neither sin nor reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r3.anchor: وروى ابن أبي رواد عنه قال: هو الربا الحلال؛ يهدي الرجل الشيء ليهدى له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r4.claim: The author links this to 74:6, revealed specifically about the Prophet and forbidding him to give a gift expecting a better one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r4.anchor: [المدثر: 6] نزلت في النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- خاصة، نهي أن يهدي هدية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r5.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says it is a gift to a brother in expectation of compensation; it does not increase with God or earn reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r5.anchor: وقال السدي: الربا في هذا الموضع: الهدية يهديها الرجل لأخيه، طلب المكافأة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r6.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says it concerns someone who gives in order to be repaid.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هذا في الرجل يعطي ليثاب عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r7.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains it as giving something to receive more in return; it is not unlawful, but brings no reward because the giver seeks an increase.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r7.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: يعني به: دفع الإنسان الشيء ليعوض ما هو أكثر منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r8.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r8.claim: Abū ʿAlī offers two parses for mā: conditional, in which it is the object of ataytum and fala yarbu is the jussive answer; or relative, nominative with an omitted pronoun and fala yarbu as predicate with fāʾ, as in 16:53.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p64/r8.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: {ما} في قوله: {وما آتيتم} يحتمل تقديرين؛ يجوز أن تكون للجزاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r1.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r1.claim: The subject of يربو is the riba mentioned earlier; an omitted noun is understood, meaning acquisition or attraction of people’s wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r1.anchor: هذا كله كلام أبي علي ذكره في مواضع متفرقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r2.speaker: نافع
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ reads لتربوا with a damma on the tāʾ: you become owners of an increase from people’s wealth by attracting it through what you give.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r3.claim: The gift does not grow with God because its giver sought increased return, not God’s good pleasure and nearness; a gift seeking God’s face would be different.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r3.anchor: لأنكم إنما قصدتم إلى زيادة العوض، ولم تقصدوا وجه البر والقربة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r4.claim: The second ما can be relative and nominative; آتيتم is its relative clause, with an omitted object pronoun understood as آتيتموه.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r4.anchor: هذا كله كلام أبي علي ذكره في مواضع متفرقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r5.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r5.claim: The wording shifts from direct address to third person, as in 10:22, moving from وما آتيتم to فأولئك.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r5.anchor: هذا كله كلام أبي علي ذكره في مواضع متفرقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r6.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r6.claim: The فاء follows because the relative clause contains a verb; the predicate is understood as you are those with multiplied reward, with a deleted resumptive pronoun, as in the idiom السمن منوان بدرهم.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r6.anchor: هذا كله كلام أبي علي ذكره في مواضع متفرقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r7.claim: Charity is given without seeking repayment and with the aim of what is with God; its people receive multiplied reward, tenfold for each good deed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r7.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وما أعطيتم من صدقة لا تطلبون بها المكافأة وإنما تقصدون بها ما عند الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r8.claim: المضعفون can mean possessors of many good deeds, like مقو meaning strong or موسر meaning wealthy: people with multiplied rewards.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r8.anchor: وكذلك: مضعف، ذو أضعاف من الحسنات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r9.claim: Muqātil introduces the following passage as describing what befell people because they abandoned monotheism.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p67/r9.anchor: قال مقاتل: ثم ذكر ما أصاب الناس من ترك التوحيد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:39/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:39/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:39/r1.claim: The riba described is a permissible gift given in expectation of receiving more back; it does not grow with God because the giver did not seek God's pleasure.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:39/r1.anchor: يعني: ما يعطونه من الهدية ليأخذوا أكثر منها، وهو من الربا الحلال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:39/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:39/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:39/r2.claim: The multipliers are those whose reward is increased tenfold for each unit given.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:39/r2.anchor: أصحاب الإضعاف، يضاعف لهم بالواحدة عشرا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r1.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says this is a gift given in expectation of receiving a better gift in return; it earns no reward but brings no sin, and the Prophet forbade it, citing 74:6.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم قال: تلك الهدية تهديها ليهدى لك خير منها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas read “liturbū”; another group read “li-yarbū,” referring to people giving gifts in hope that more will be given back.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r2.anchor: أنه سمع ابن عباس قرأها: لتربوا وبعضهم يقرأها: ليربوا، أي: ليربوا ذلك الربا الذي يربون

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r3.claim: The word riba means increase: people give to others hoping those recipients will give them more.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r3.anchor: والربا الزيادة، أي: يهدون إلى الناس ليهدوا إليكم أكثر منه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r4.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r4.claim: The Prophet says a gift is provision from God; whoever receives one should accept it and give something better in return.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r4.anchor: الهدية رزق الله فمن أهدي إليه شيء، فليقبله وليعط خيرا منه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r5.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r5.claim: The Prophet says no one should refuse a gift from a fellow Muslim, but should give a gift in return as he was given one.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p661/r5.anchor: لا يردن أحدكم على أخيه الهدية وليهد له كما أهدي له

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p662/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p662/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p662/r1.claim: Al-Suddi explains giving zakah seeking God's face as giving it in pursuit of God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p662/r1.anchor: يريد: تريدون به الله: وهو تفسير السدي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p662/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p662/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p662/r2.claim: Those who give for God are the ones for whom God multiplies the reward.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p662/r2.anchor: يعني: الذين يضاعف الله تبارك وتعالى لهم الحساب.

ELMALILI:30:39-40/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r1.claim: Elmalılı prefers the apparent meaning of ribā as familiar interest or usury, rather than a figurative sense.
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r1.anchor: Bazıları bundan murad, mâruf olan ribâ, yani faiz olduğunu söylemişlerdir ki zâhir olan da budur.

ELMALILI:30:39-40/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r2.speaker: Süddî
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r2.claim: Al-Suddi reports that the verse concerned the usury of Thaqif; since Thaqif and Quraysh practiced usury, it censured interest before its later prohibition.
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r2.anchor: Nitekim Süddî bu âyetin Sakīf’in ribâsı hakkında nâzil olduğunu rivayet eylemiştir.

ELMALILI:30:39-40/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r3.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r3.claim: Many exegetes, on a meaning transmitted from Ibn Abbas, take ribā figuratively as gifts given while expecting a greater return; the comparison censures such gifts like usury and more strongly implies usury’s prohibition.
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r3.anchor: fazla hediyeler, atıyyeler olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır ki bu mâna İbn Abbas’tan mervîdir.

ELMALILI:30:39-40/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r4.claim: On the gift interpretation, expecting extra repayment earns no reward, though the gift itself is not sinful; actual usury likewise has no reward with God.
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r4.anchor: Gerçi bu günah değildir, fakat sevâbı da yoktur.

ELMALILI:30:39-40/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r5.claim: Alms given seeking God’s pleasure are the true multipliers, and their reward is multiplied as in the grain yielding seven ears with a hundred grains each.
ELMALILI:30:39-40/r5.anchor: Allah yüzünü, Allah rızâsını murad ederek verdiğiniz zekât ise

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r1.claim: Verses 37–40 move from differences in people's means to social assistance, God's disapproval of exploitative ribā, and a renewed affirmation of divine unity, echoing the parable in verse 28.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r1.anchor: insanların farklı imkânlara sahip olmaları, özellikle iktisadî bakımdan farklı seviyelerde bulunmaları realitesine yine onların gözlemleri tanık tutul

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r15.claim: Verse 39 first signals the Qur'an's firm opposition to ribā, which harms economic justice and society, by comparing ribā with zakat through the motives behind each.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r15.anchor: iktisadî adaleti temelden sarsan ve toplumda büyük tahribat yapan ribâ uygulamalarına karşı Allah’ın Kur’an’da kesin bir tavır takınacağının ilk işareti verilmiş, bu yapılırken insanların ribâdaki amacına atıfta bulunularak zekâtla bir mukayese yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r16.claim: A person seeking to increase wealth through ribā should know that gains from exploiting others are only apparent material growth, without spiritual increase or blessing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r16.anchor: başkalarının sömürülmesi esasına dayalı bir işlemle elde edilecek kazanç zâhirî bir artıştır, mânevî yönden bir artış değildir, bereketi de yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r17.claim: The real investment is spending in ways pleasing to God, especially zakat in its broad sense.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r17.anchor: Gerçek yatırım Allah’ın hoşnutluğuna uygun harcamalarda bulunmaktır ki bunların başında geniş anlamıyla zekât gelmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r19.claim: The first sentence can alternatively mean that wealth or trade involving ribā does not grow or become blessed, yielding the rendering that the ribā given to increase people's wealth does not increase with God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r19.anchor: 39. âyetin ilk cümlesini, “İçine ribânın girdiği bir servet ve ticaret, artmaz, bereketli olmaz” şeklinde yorumlamak da mümkündür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r20.speaker: Taberî, Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r20.claim: Some exegetes, noting that the verse contains no explicit prohibition, take ribā here as non-prohibited dealings with no value before God, especially gifts made expecting thanks or some benefit.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r20.anchor: Bazı müfessirler burada bir yasak ifadesinin bulunmamasından hareketle bu kelimeyi haram olmayan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r21.claim: For the scope and stages of the ribā prohibition and the growth of zakat and charity versus ribā, the author points to al-Baqara 2:275–276 and Āl ʿImrān 3:130.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:37/r21.anchor: ribânın kapsamı, İslâm’da ribâ yasağıyla ilgili süreç, zekât ve sadakanın artması fakat ribânın artmaması hakkında bilgi için bk. Bakara 2/275-276; Âl-i İmrân 3/130

BURHAN:v1p409/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p409/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p409/r1.claim: The orthographic convention writes alif as waw in four core words and four derivative forms, reflecting emphatic pronunciation.
BURHAN:v1p409/r1.anchor: وذلك فى أربعة أصول مطردة وأربعة أحرف متفرعة

BURHAN:v1p409/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p409/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p409/r2.claim: Prayer and zakat are Islam's pillars, life is the soul's basis and key to survival, and avoiding riba is a basis of security and a key to piety.
BURHAN:v1p409/r2.anchor: فإن الصلاة والزكاة عمودا الإسلام والحياة قاعدة النفس ومفتاح البقاء

BURHAN:v1p409/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p409/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p409/r3.claim: Riba contains forbidden and corrupt forms, opposes zakat, and avoiding it is foundational to financial conduct; the Qur'an pairs its erasure with the growth of charities.
BURHAN:v1p409/r3.anchor: ويشتمل على أنواع الحرام وأنواع الخبائث وضروب المفاسد وهو نقيض الزكاة

BURHAN:v1p409/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p409/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p409/r4.claim: Riba is written with alif here because the verse does not refer to the universal category prohibited by God; negating a universal negates all its instances.
BURHAN:v1p409/r4.anchor: فى سورة الروم لأنه ليس العام الكلى لأن الكلى منفى فى حكم الله عليه بالتحريم

BURHAN:v1p409/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p409/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p409/r5.claim: Zakat is written with waw because the verse intends the universal category in God's judgment, as shown by the promise of multiplied reward.
BURHAN:v1p409/r5.anchor: قلت لأن المراد بها الكلية فى حكم الله ولذلك قال ﴿ فأولئك هم المضعفون ﴾

ITQAN:v3p231/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p231/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p231/r1.claim: Iltifat shifts from direct address to third person in the zakat phrase, as well as in examples from al-Hujurat and al-Zukhruf; al-Zukhruf shifts back to direct address.
ITQAN:v3p231/r1.anchor: ومن أمثلته أيضا ﴿ وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون ﴾ ﴿ وكره إليكم الكفر والفسوق والعصيان أولئك هم الراشدون ﴾

NAHHAS:v3p274/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p274/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p274/r9.claim: Scholars explain this as a gift given expecting repayment rather than God's reward; it is permissible but earns no divine recompense.
NAHHAS:v3p274/r9.anchor: قول العلماء فيه أنه أن يهدي الرجل إلى الرجل الهدية يريد عليها المكافأة ولا يريد الثواب فذلك مباح

NAHHAS:v3p274/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p274/r10.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v3p274/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says the Prophet specifically forbade this practice, citing the command not to give in order to receive more.
NAHHAS:v3p274/r10.anchor: غير أن الضحاك قال نهى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذلك خاصة بقوله

NAHHAS:v3p274/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p274/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p274/r11.claim: Another interpretation takes الربا here to mean prohibited usury.
NAHHAS:v3p274/r11.anchor: وقد قيل معنى وما آتيتم من ربا هو الربا الذي لا يحل

NAHHAS:v3p274/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p274/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p274/r12.claim: On the usury interpretation, God does not validate the excess for its taker because it belongs to the person from whom it was taken.
NAHHAS:v3p274/r12.anchor: فلا يربو عند الله فلا يحكم به لآخذه لأنه ليس له وإنما هو للمأخوذ منه

NAHHAS:v3p274/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p274/r13.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v3p274/r13.claim: Sibawayh gives the dual of ربا as ربوان; his associates permit no other form.
NAHHAS:v3p274/r13.anchor: وتثنية الربا ربوان كذا قول سيبويه ولا يجوز عند أصحابه غيره

NAHHAS:v3p274/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p274/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p274/r14.claim: Al-Nahhas sides with Abu Ishaq against the Kufian spelling and dual, since ليربو clearly shows a waw-root.
NAHHAS:v3p274/r14.anchor: فهذا أبين أنه من ذوات الواو وأن القول كما قال أبو إسحاق

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r3.claim: Arabic and Qurʾanic speech may address listeners in the second person and then refer to them in the third person.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r3.anchor: ومنه أن تخاطب الشاهد بشيء ثم تجعل الخطاب له على لفظ الغائب

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r1.claim: Ribā names both money lent at interest and the interest charged; Islahi rejects the gloss “gift” and explains it as naming something by its consequence, citing Yūsuf 12:36 and his essay.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r1.anchor: Those who regard it to mean a gift are absolutely wrong. This word is used in accordance with the linguistic principle of Arabic

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r2.claim: Here zakāh is not a technical term but means charity (ṣadaqāt), a usage found elsewhere in the Qur’an.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r2.anchor: The word ٍةو ٰکَز here does not occur here as a term. It refers to charity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r3.claim: The verse contrasts the prior call to give: interest-based lending extracts from others and does not grow with God, whereas wealth spent to please God does.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r3.anchor: Only that wealth increases with God which is spent in His way to please Him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r4.claim: Islahi likens interest wealth to an ox fattened by grazing on others’ land; it lacks blessing, unlike earnings from one’s own field spent to fulfill rights and please God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r4.anchor: God has compared the wealth of an interest-charger to an ox that grows fat by grazing on the lands of others

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r5.claim: The rate at which wealth given in God’s way increases is detailed elsewhere in the Qur’an.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r5.anchor: The rate of this increase has been mentioned in detail at another instance in the Qur’ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r6.claim: Fear of the future drives wealth accumulation, but people see only their worldly future and miss the Hereafter; investing with God secures wealth for eternal life.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r6.anchor: He is not able to see the real future which is the Hereafter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r7.claim: Permissible business capital grows within its own risky investment, whereas a moneylender hides like an ambush and profitably draws from the needy without taking risks.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p85/r7.anchor: the capital of a tradesman or a businessman after braving many dangers and different circumstances increases from its own circle of investment

IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r12.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r12.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r12.claim: Ibn Kathir reads آتيتم in the riba phrase without lengthening; the other readers lengthen it.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r12.anchor: كلهم قرأ / ءاتيتم / ممدودة غير ابن كثير فإنه قرأ ﴿ آتيتم ﴾ مقصورة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r13.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r13.speaker: الباقون
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r13.claim: All readers except Ibn Kathir lengthen آتيتم in the riba phrase.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r13.anchor: كلهم قرأ / ءاتيتم / ممدودة غير ابن كثير فإنه قرأ ﴿ آتيتم ﴾ مقصورة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r14.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r14.speaker: القراء
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r14.claim: The readers agree on lengthening آتيتم in the zakāt phrase.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r14.anchor: ولم يختلفوا فى مد ﴿ وما آتيتم من زكاة ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r15.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r15.speaker: القراء
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r15.claim: All readers other than Nafi read ليربوا with yāʾ and an open wāw.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r15.anchor: كلهم قرأ / ليربوا / بالياء مفتوحة الواو غير نافع

IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r16.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r16.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r16.claim: Nafi reads لتربوا with tāʾ and a silent wāw.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r16.anchor: غير نافع فإنه قرأ / لتربوا / بضم التاء ساكنة الواو

NASHR:v2p227/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p227/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v2p227/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir shortens the hamza in the phrase here and in the first al-Rum occurrence, from the sense of coming or doing; the others lengthen it for the sense of giving.
NASHR:v2p227/r3.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير بقصر الهمزة فيهما من باب المجيء، وقرأ الباقون بالمد من باب الإعطاء

NASHR:v2p227/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p227/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p227/r4.claim: Readers agree on lengthening the second al-Rum phrase because it means giving; the shortened forms mean doing or intending, unlike the passive sense of receiving.
NASHR:v2p227/r4.anchor: وهو قوله تعالى: وما آتيتم من زكاة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r9.claim: The ring gift shows voluntary alms can be called zakat; 30:39 includes obligatory and voluntary giving, as do sadaqa and salat.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:55/r9.anchor: وقوله: { ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون } يدل على أن صدقة التطوع تسمى زكاة فإن عليا تصدق بخاتمه

BURHAN:v3p318/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p318/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p318/r5.claim: The author lists charity given for God's sake and God making disbelief and sin hateful as further examples of shifting from address to third person.
BURHAN:v3p318/r5.anchor: وقوله ﴿ وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون ﴾
